mekki-muskil:186-186.t: His saying {أُجِيب دَعْوَة}: a second khabar (predicate) of «لآن» [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently «لإنّ», i.e. of إنّ in ﴿فَإِنِّي قَرِيبٌ﴾], and قَرِيب is the first khabar.

mekki-muskil:187-187.t:
His saying {لَيْلَة الصّيام الرَّفَث}: لَيْلَة is a ẓarf (adverb of time) for الرفث, which is sexual intercourse, and the governing word (ʿāmil) in it is أحل; and الرفث is the object whose agent is not named [Translator's note: i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)].
His saying {وَأَنْتُم عاكفون فِي الْمَسَاجِد}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative implied pronoun in تباشروهن.

mekki-muskil:188-188.t:
His saying {وتدلوا} بهَا: jussive (majzūm) by conjunction with تَأْكُلُوا. It is also permissible for تدلوا to be accusative (manṣūb), making it a response to the prohibition with the wāw.
His saying {وَأَنْتُم تعلمُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative implied pronoun in لتأكلوا [Translator's note: so in the source; the verse has لِتَأْكُلُوا].

mekki-muskil:189-189.t: {وَلَكِن الْبر من اتَّقى}: like the first one in all its aspects. As for his saying وَلَيْسَ الْبر بِأَن تَأْتُوا, nothing is permissible in الْبر except the nominative (rafʿ), because of the entry of the bāʾ into the khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:196-196.t: His saying {فَمَا اسْتَيْسَرَ من الْهَدْي}: مَا is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "then upon him is مَا اسْتَيْسَرَ". It is also permissible for it to be in the position of the accusative, on the implied form "let him offer (فليهد) مَا اسْتَيْسَرَ".

mekki-muskil:197-197.t:
His saying {الْحَج أشهر مَعْلُومَات}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). In the speech there is an omission of a muḍāf, so that the subject is the predicate in meaning; its implied form is "the months of the Hajj are known months". Were it not for this implication (iḍmār), the analogy would be the accusative of أشهر as a ẓarf (adverb), as you say "the fighting is today (الْقِتَال الْيَوْم)" and "the going out is at this hour (وَالْخُرُوج السَّاعَة)".
His saying {فَلَا رفث وَلَا فسوق}: whoever reads it in the accusative does so on the basis of tabriʾa (the lā of generic negation), like لَا ريب فِيهِ; and whoever reads it in the nominative makes لَا in the sense of لَيْسَ, and the khabar of لَيْسَ is omitted, i.e. "there is no رفث in it".

mekki-muskil:198-198.t:
His saying {عَرَفَات}: the readers are unanimous on giving it tanwīn, because it is a name of a place. The analogy of grammar is that if you named a woman مسلمات you would leave the tanwīn as it is and not drop it, because it did not enter this noun as a distinction between what is declinable and what is not declinable (a diptote), and it need not be dropped when it is the name of something diptote; it is only like a letter of the root. Sībawayh reported that some of the Arabs drop the tanwīn from عَرَفَات: when they made it a definite proper name they dropped the tanwīn and left the tāʾ with kasra in the accusative and the genitive. Al-Akhfash and the Kufans reported a fatḥa on the tāʾ without tanwīn in the accusative and the genitive; they treated it like the hāʾ of the feminine in فَاطِمَة and عَائِشَة.
His saying {كَمَا هدَاكُمْ} and كذكركم آبَاءَكُم: the kāf in both is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a remembrance as (كَمَا)…" and "a remembrance like your remembrance (كذكركم)". It is also permissible for the kāf in كذكركم to be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in فاذكروا, i.e. "remember Him, resembling your remembrance of your fathers".

mekki-muskil:200-200.t:
His saying {أَو أَشد ذكرا}: أَشد is in the position of the genitive, conjoined to كذكركم. It is also permissible for it to be accusative on an implied verb, its implied form being "and remember (Him) with a remembrance more intense in remembrance than your remembrance of your fathers"; it would then be a naʿt (adjective) of a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "remember Him, going to great lengths in remembering Him".
His saying لمن اتَّقى: the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) "forgiveness", i.e. "forgiveness is for whoever guards against game (الصَّيْد)" [Translator's note: so in the source]. It was said that its implied form is "the permission in it, in delaying and hastening, is for whoever is mindful"; it was said "safety is for whoever is mindful"; and it was said "remembrance is for whoever is mindful".

mekki-muskil:204-204.t: His saying {أَلد الْخِصَام}: it (الْخِصَام) is the plural of خصم; and it was said that it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of خَاصم.

mekki-muskil:208-208.t: His saying {كَافَّة}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ادخُلُوا. Its meaning is: none of you refrains from entering, i.e. some of you restrain (يكف) others from refraining.

mekki-muskil:211-211.t:
His saying {كم آتَيْنَاهُم}: كم is in the position of the accusative by an implied verb after it, its implied form being "how many have We given, We gave them". His saying من آيَة is in the position of the second object of آتيناهم. It is also permissible to make كم a second object of آتيناهم. And if you wish, you may put it in the position of the nominative on the implication of a returning pronoun, its implied form being "how many We gave them it (أتيناهموه)"; there is weakness in this because of the dropping of the hāʾ, and it is like your saying "which of them have I given you it (أَيهَا أعطيتكه)", so you put it in the nominative; but the preferred choice is the accusative by an implied verb after أي, its implied form being "which of them have I given you, I gave it to you". The nominative with the dropping of the hāʾ is ugly, and Sībawayh did not allow it except in poetry.
It is not permissible for سل to govern كم, because what precedes an interrogative does not govern it. So the nominative in كم is far-fetched because of the dropping of the hāʾ, and what precedes كم, namely سل, does not govern it, because it has the head of the sentence (ṣadr al-kalām), since it is an interrogative, and what precedes the interrogative does not govern it. من entered with كم, while it is interrogative, only to distinguish between it and the accusative. And كم is an indeclinable noun because of its resemblance to particles, since it is used to ask questions just as the alif is used to ask questions. If you dropped من you would put آيَة in the accusative as tafsīr (specification), when you make كم a second object of آتيناهم.

mekki-muskil:213-213.t:
His saying {مبشرين} and منذرين: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from النَّبِيين.
His saying {بغيا بَينهم}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:214-214.t:
His saying {أَن تدْخلُوا الْجنَّة}: أَن (with its clause) is in the position of the two objects of حسب.
His saying {حَتَّى}: it is written with yāʾ because it resembles سكرى, and Nuṣayr reported imāla (inclination of the vowel) of it from al-Kisāʾī. It is written only with yāʾ because it resembles إِلَى. And إِمَّا is not written with yāʾ by analogy with حَتَّى, because it is أَن to which مَا has been joined.
His saying {حَتَّى يَقُول الرَّسُول}: whoever reads يَقُول in the nominative does so because it is an action that has gone and ended, and the report is only about the state that the Messenger was in in the past; so the verb indicates the state they were in in the past. Thus حتى enters upon a sentence in meaning, and it does not govern sentences. It is permissible in speech to read it in the nominative and report about the state he is in now, as in your saying "he fell ill until they no longer have hope for him (مرض حَتَّى لَا يرجونه)", i.e. he fell ill in the past until now he is not hoped for; so you narrate the state he is in, and there is no way to the accusative in this meaning. If you put it in the accusative, the meaning would be reversed and you would be reporting two actions that have passed and gone, and you would not be narrating a state he was in. Its implied form is that you narrate a state the Prophet was in, so its implied form is "and they were shaken until the Messenger said", as you say "I travelled until I enter it (سرت حَتَّى أدخلها)", i.e. I had travelled and then entered; so حتى comes to enter upon a sentence, and it does not govern sentences, hence the verb after it is nominative and it does not govern it.
As for the reasoning of whoever reads it in the accusative: he made حتى a particle of limit in the sense of إِلَى أَن, so he put it in the accusative by an implied أن, and made the saying of the Messenger, upon him be peace, the limit of his Companions' fear, because زلزلوا means "they were made to fear"; so its meaning is "and they were shaken until the Messenger said", and the two actions have both passed.
His saying {أَلا إِن نصر الله قريب}: قريب is the khabar (predicate) of إن. قَرِيبا is also permissible, making it a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted ẓarf (adverb), i.e. "a near place"; in this meaning it is not made dual, plural or feminine. If you say "it is near me (هُوَ قريب مني)" meaning the place, it is not made dual, plural or feminine; but if you mean kinship, you make it dual, plural and feminine.

mekki-muskil:215-215.t:
His saying {يَسْأَلُونَك مَاذَا يُنْفقُونَ}: مَا is interrogative, and for that reason يَسْأَلُونَك does not govern it; so it is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and ذَا is in the sense of الَّذِي and it is the khabar (predicate). The hāʾ is omitted from يُنْفقُونَ because of the length of the noun, since it is the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّذِي; its implied form is "they ask you: what is the thing that they spend (ينفقونه)?". And if you wish, you may make مَا and ذَا a single noun, so that مَا is in the position of the accusative governed by ينفقون, and you do not imply an omitted hāʾ, as though you said "they ask you: what thing do they spend?".
His saying {قل مَا أنفقتم}: مَا is conditional, in the position of the accusative governed by أنفقتم, and likewise وَمَا تنفقوا; and the fāʾ is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition in both.

mekki-muskil:217-217.t:
His saying {قتال فِيهِ}: قتال is a badal (substitute) from الشَّهْر, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). Al-Kisāʾī said it is genitive by repetition (takrīr); its implied form according to him is "about the month, about fighting in it". Likewise al-Farrāʾ said it is genitive by an implied عَن. Abū ʿUbayda said it is genitive by proximity (ʿalā al-jiwār).
His saying {وَصد عَن سَبِيل الله}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); and كفر and إخراج are conjoined to صد, and أكبر عِنْد الله is its khabar (predicate). Al-Farrāʾ said that صد and كفر are conjoined to كَبِير; that would require that fighting in the sacred month is disbelief. Moreover, after it comes "and expelling its people from it is greater with Allah", and it is impossible that expelling the people of the Sacred Mosque from it should be greater with Allah than disbelief in Allah. It was said that الصد is nominative as mubtadaʾ, كفر is conjoined to it, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "great (كَبِير) with Allah" [Translator's note: the source reads «كَبِير أَن عِنْد الله»], because the first khabar indicates it. On this view it would follow that expelling the people of the Sacred Mosque from it is greater with Allah than disbelief, whereas expelling them from it is only one of the traits of disbelief.
His saying {وَالْمَسْجِد الْحَرَام}: conjoined to سَبِيل الله, i.e. fighting in the sacred month is a great (sin), and it is barring from the way of Allah and from the Mosque. Al-Farrāʾ said that المسجد is conjoined to الشَّهْر الْحَرَام; there is remoteness in this, because their question was not about the Sacred Mosque; they only asked about the sacred month, whether fighting is permissible in it. So they were told: fighting in it is a great sin, but barring from the way of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque, disbelief in Allah, and expelling the people of the Sacred Mosque from it are greater in sin with Allah than fighting in the sacred month. Then they were told: "and fitna is greater than killing", i.e. the disbelief in Allah that you are upon, O questioners, is graver in sin than killing in the sacred month about which you asked and which you condemned. This interpretation makes clear the i'rab of this verse.

mekki-muskil:219-220.t:
His saying {مَاذَا يُنْفقُونَ قل الْعَفو}: it is like the first one, except that if you make ذَا in the sense of الَّذِي you put الْعَفو in the nominative, because مَا is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), so its answer is nominative like it; and you imply the hāʾ with يُنْفقُونَ, referring back to the relative noun, and it is dropped because of the length of the noun. If you make مَا and ذَا a single noun in the position of the accusative governed by ينفقون, you put الْعَفو in the accusative, because it is the answer to مَا, so its i'rab must be like its i'rab, and you do not imply a hāʾ.
His saying {تتفكرون فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَة}: فِي is attached to (mutaʿalliq) تتفكرون, so they (this world and the Hereafter) are two containers (ẓarfs) for the reflection; its implied form is "you reflect on the affairs of this world and the Hereafter and their consequences". It was said that فِي is attached to يبين, its implied form being "thus Allah makes clear to you the signs concerning the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, that you may reflect". The kāf of كَذَلِك is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "with a making-clear like that Allah makes clear to you the signs".
His saying {فإخوانكم}: the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "then they are your brothers".
His saying {الْمُفْسد من المصلح}: two generic nouns; the alif and lām did not enter them for definiteness, but entered only for the genus, as you say "the dinar and the dirham have ruined people" and as in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إِن الْإِنْسَان لفي خسر﴾: He did not mean a specific dinar, nor a specific dirham, nor a specific human being; you meant only this genus. Likewise the meaning of His saying الْمُفْسد من المصلح is: He knows these two kinds.

mekki-muskil:224-224.t: His saying {أَن تبروا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative, in the sense of "in that you be righteous (فِي أَن تبروا)"; when the preposition was dropped, the verb became transitive [Translator's note: i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition]. It was said its implied form is "out of dislike that (كَرَاهَة أَن)", and it was said "so that not (لِئَلَّا)". Al-Kisāʾī said the position of أَن is genitive by an implied genitive-governing particle. It is also permissible for its position to be nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being "that you be righteous, be mindful and make peace between people is more fitting" or "better".

mekki-muskil:229-229.t:
His saying {الطَّلَاق مَرَّتَانِ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); its implied form is "the number of divorces after which taking back (rajʿa) is obligatory [Translator's note: so in the source] is two".
His saying {فإمساك بِمَعْرُوف}: a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "then upon you is retaining"; and likewise أَو تَسْرِيح بِإِحْسَان. If it were put in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) outside the Quran, it would be permissible.
His saying {إِلَّا أَن يخافا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative, an exception not of the first kind (i.e. disjoined exception).
His saying {أَلا يُقِيمَا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative because of the absence of the preposition; its implied form is "of (مِن) their not keeping", "in (بِ) their not keeping" and "on (عَلَى) their not keeping".

mekki-muskil:231-231.t: His saying {ضِرَارًا}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

mekki-muskil:232-232.t: His saying {أَن ينكحن}: أَن is in the position of the accusative governed by تعضلوهن, i.e. do not prevent them from marrying their husbands.

mekki-muskil:233-233.t: His saying {لَا تضار وَالِدَة}: وَالِدَة is the object whose agent is not named [Translator's note: i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], and تضار is in the sense of تضارر (passive). It is also permissible for it to be nominative by its verb (as fāʿil, agent), on the basis that تضار is of the pattern تفاعل, its origin being تضارر, and an omitted object is implied; its implied form is "and let no mother harm (تضارر) the father through her child, nor a father harm the mother through his child". وعَلى الْوَارِث مثل ذَلِك: i.e. upon the heir of the child is that he not harm his mother nor his father. And it was said its meaning is: upon the heir is spending on the child.

mekki-muskil:234-234.t: His saying {وَالَّذين يتوفون مِنْكُم ويذرون أَزْوَاجًا}: الَّذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and there is disagreement about the implied form of the khabar (predicate) of the subject, because of the absence of anything in its khabar referring back to the subject. Al-Akhfash said the khabar is يَتَرَبَّصْنَ, and in the speech there is an omission of the pronoun referring back to the subject; its implied form is "they (the wives) wait by themselves after them" or "after their death"; then it was omitted, since it is known that waiting is only after the death of the husbands. Al-Kisāʾī said the implied form of the khabar is "their wives wait". Al-Mubarrad said the implied form is "and leave wives, their wives wait by themselves". It was said that the omission is only at the beginning of the speech, its implied form being "and the wives of those of you who die wait by themselves". And the analogy of Sībawayh's view is that the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "among what is recited to you: those of you who die…", like السَّارِق والسارقة.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
The words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: {الم} are disjointed letters (aḥruf muqaṭṭaʿa), cited as they are (maḥkiyya), and not declined unless you predicate something of them or conjoin some of them to others, so you say «هَذَا ألف» (this is an alif) and «ألفك حَسَنَة» (your alif is fine), and «فِي الْكتاب ألف وَلَام وَمِيم وَعين» (in the book there are an alif, a lām, a mīm and an ʿayn). The position of الم is accusative in the sense of "أَقرَأ الم" (I recite Alif Lām Mīm). Its position may be nominative in the sense of "هَذَا الم" (this is Alif Lām Mīm), or "ذَلِك", or "هُوَ". Its position may be genitive in the view of whoever makes it an oath. Al-Farrāʾ makes الم a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ذَلِك the khabar (predicate); its implied form according to him is "the letters of the alphabet, O Muḥammad, are that Book"; al-Zajjāj rejected this.

ذَلِك is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, or as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar implied. ذَا is a vague (mubham), indeclinable (mabnī) noun. According to the Kufans the noun is the dhāl, and the alif was added to make the vowel clear and to strengthen it; according to the Basrans ذَا as a whole is the noun. Its plural is أولاء. The lām is a lām of emphasis (lām al-taʾkīd) that entered to indicate the remoteness of what is pointed to; it is also said that it entered to indicate that ذَا is not muḍāf (in genitive construct) to the kāf. The lām was given kasra to distinguish it from the lām of possession when you say «ذَا لَك», i.e. "this is in your possession"; it is also said that it was given kasra because it is vowelless and the alif before it is vowelless.

The kāf is for address and has no position in i'rab, because it must be either in the position of the nominative, the accusative or the genitive. It cannot be in the position of the nominative, because there is nothing before it to make it nominative, and the kāf is not one of the signs of the nominative pronoun. It cannot be in the position of the accusative, since there is no operator before it to make it accusative. It cannot be in the position of the genitive, because what comes before it — the vague noun — does not take a muḍāf ilayhi. Since the three possibilities are void, it is known that it is for address and has no position in i'rab.

الْكتاب is a badal (substitute) for ذَا, or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or the khabar of ذَلِك.

mekki-muskil:235-235.t:
His saying {وَلَكِن لَا تواعدوهن سرا}: i.e. "on a secret", i.e. on marriage. If you take it from السِّرّ in the sense of concealment, it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تواعدوهن; its implied form is "but do not promise them marriage, acting in secret and not making it open".
His saying {إِلَّا أَن تَقولُوا قولا مَعْرُوفا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative, an exception not of the first kind (i.e. disjoined exception).
His saying {وَلَا تعزموا عقدَة النِّكَاح}: i.e. "on (عَلَى) the knot of marriage"; when the preposition was dropped it was put in the accusative, as you say "Zayd was struck the back and the belly (ضرب زيد الظّهْر والبطن)", i.e. on the back and the belly. It was said that عقدَة is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), and تعزموا is in the sense of تعقدوا.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His words {لَا ريب فِيهِ}: لَا is the lā of exoneration (tabriʾa, i.e. the lā of generic negation), so it and ريب are like a single noun; that is why ريب is made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, because with لَا it is like خمسة عشر (fifteen). It is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of ذَلِك.

His words {هدى} are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ذَا, or from الْكتاب, or from the nominative pronoun implied in فِيهِ. The operator on it, if it is a ḥāl from ذَا or from الْكتاب, is the meaning of pointing; if it is a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in فِيهِ, the operator on it is the meaning of being settled (istiqrār). It is also permitted that هدى be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with فِيهِ as the khabar; on this view you pause at لَا ريب. It may also be nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, or as the khabar of ذَلِك, or as a khabar after a khabar.

His words {لِلْمُتقين}: its pattern is المفتعلين and its original form is الموتقيين. Then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ, so it became a doubled yāʾ [Translator's note: as written; in the morphology of اتّقى the wāw is turned into tāʾ and assimilated into the tāʾ of iftiʿāl, as the author himself says at 2:21, so «tāʾ» is probably intended]. The first yāʾ was made vowelless because the kasra on it was felt to be heavy, then it was dropped because it was vowelless and the yāʾ of the plural after it was vowelless.

mekki-muskil:236-236.t: His saying {مَتَاعا}: accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it was said a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His words {الَّذين يُؤمنُونَ بِالْغَيْبِ}: الَّذين is in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of لِلْمُتقين, or a badal (substitute) for them; or in the position of the accusative by an implied أَعنِي (I mean); or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar (predicate) is أُولَئِكَ على هدى من رَبهم.

The original form of يُؤمنُونَ is يؤأمنون with two hamzas, the first with fatḥa, and it is the augment; the augment was dropped because of the meeting of two hamzas in it, and the meeting of three hamzas when speaking of oneself (the first person). They extended this dropping to all the verbs that follow the four-letter pattern, even where two hamzas do not meet, as in يكرم and يلهي — just as they said يعد, dropping the wāw because it falls between a yāʾ and a kasra, and then extended that to the rest of the category even where there is no yāʾ, as in تعد and تزن; and just as they introduced هُوَ, أَنْت and the like as a separating pronoun (fāṣila) between the khabar and the naʿt in your saying «إِن زيدا هُوَ الْعَاقِل» and «كَانَ زيد هُوَ الْعَاقِل», and then introduced them as separators where a naʿt is impossible, as in «زيد كَانَ هُوَ الْعَاقِل» and «كنت أَنْت الْعَاقِل»; and just as they introduced the pronoun of the unknown (al-majhūl, i.e. the pronoun of the matter) with أَن and كَانَ when what follows them is something that cannot directly follow them and that they do not govern, as in «أَنه قَامَ زيد», «كَانَ يقوم عمر» and «كَانَ لَا أحد فِي الدَّار», and then extended that to the rest of the category even where that reason is absent, saying «أَنه زيد قَائِم». The original form of يُؤمنُونَ and the like had to have two hamzas because these augment letters ought properly to contain what was in the past tense, and the past tense had two hamzas, the first being the augment, namely your saying أأمن. On this basis whatever resembles it is measured, and its reason is the same reason, so measure it accordingly.

His words {يُقِيمُونَ}: its original form is يؤقومون. The hamza was dropped, then the vowel of the wāw was cast onto the qāf, which took kasra, and the wāw turned into yāʾ because it was vowelless and the letter before it had kasra. Its pattern is يَفْعَلُونَ [Translator's note: as written; the intended pattern is presumably يُفْعِلُونَ], like يُؤمنُونَ.

His words {الصَّلَاة}: its original form is صلوة, as shown by their saying صلوَات; so its pattern is فعلة.

mekki-muskil:237-237.t: His saying {فَنصف مَا فرضتم}: نصف is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "then upon you is half of what you appointed". If it were put in the accusative in ordinary speech, it would be permissible in the sense of "then pay half of what you appointed".

mekki-muskil:5-5.t:
His words {أُولَئِكَ} are the khabar (predicate) of {الَّذين}, or a mubtadaʾ (subject) if you do not make الَّذين a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar being على هدى. هدى is a shortened (maqṣūr), fully declinable (munṣarif) noun whose pattern is فعل; its original form is هدي. When the yāʾ was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, it was turned into alif; the alif is vowelless and the tanwīn is vowelless, so the alif was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and the tanwīn came to follow the fatḥa of the dāl, so it does not change in any case. The same reason applies to everything like it.

أُولَئِكَ is a vague (mubham) noun for a group; it is indeclinable (mabnī) on kasra and does not change. It was made indeclinable because it resembles the particles. The kāf is for address and has no position in i'rab. The singular of أُولَئِكَ is ذَلِك; and when it is for the feminine, its singular is ذِي, تي and ذه [Translator's note: the edition reads «ذِي أُوتِيَ أوذه», evidently a corruption of «ذِي أو تي أو ذه» (ذي, or تي, or ذه)].

mekki-muskil:240-240.t:
His saying {وَالَّذين يتوفون مِنْكُم}: الَّذين is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "they make a bequest (وَصِيَّة)". If you read وَصِيَّة in the nominative, its implied form is "then upon them is a bequest": you put وَصِيَّة in the nominative as mubtadaʾ, the implied عَلَيْهِم is its khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of الَّذين.
His saying {مَتَاعا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to al-Akhfash, and a ḥāl (circumstantial) according to al-Mubarrad, on the implied form "possessors of provision".
His saying {غير إِخْرَاج}: he put غير in the accusative as a maṣdar according to al-Akhfash, its implied form being "no expelling"; then غير was put in the place of لَا, and it was given the i'rab that what it is annexed to, namely الْإِخْرَاج, would have. It was said that غير is accusative because of the dropping of the preposition: its implied form was "without (من غير) expelling", and when من was dropped it became accusative the way the direct object is accusative. It was said that غير is accusative as a ḥāl from those who bequeath, the ones who die; its implied form is "provision for a year, not being people of expelling", or "not expelling them".

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His words {سَوَاء عَلَيْهِم} are a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it, the mention of warning, is its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of إِن. الَّذين is the noun (ism) of إِن and its ṣila (relative clause) is كفرُوا. The alif of أأنذرتهم is the alif of equivalence (taswiya), because it established that warning and not warning are the same for those for whom wretchedness was decreed beforehand in the knowledge of Allah: they will never believe. Its form is the form of the interrogative, and that is why أم came after it. It is also permitted that سَوَاء be the khabar of إِن and what follows it be in the position of the nominative by its verb-like operator, namely سَوَاء. It is also permitted that the khabar of إِن be لَا يُؤمنُونَ.

mekki-muskil:241-241.t: His saying {حَقًا}: a maṣdar (verbal noun); and عَلَى is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied verb that puts حَقًا in the accusative.

mekki-muskil:7-7.t: His words {وعَلى سمعهم}: it was only made singular, and not plural as القلوب and الْأَبْصَار were made plural, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said that its implied form is "وعَلى مَوَاضِع سمعهم" (and upon the places of their hearing). His words غشاوة are nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is على أَبْصَارهم; the pause at سمعهم is good. ʿĀṣim read it in the accusative, by an implied verb, as though He said "وَجعل على أَبْصَارهم غشاوة" (and He placed a covering over their eyes); the pause at سمعهم is permitted in this reading, but is not as good as in the reading of those who read the nominative.

mekki-muskil:245-245.t:
His saying {من ذَا الَّذِي يقْرض الله}: من is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ذَا is its khabar (predicate); الَّذِي is a naʿt (adjective) of ذا or a badal (substitute) from it. Similar is مَن ذَا الَّذِي يشفع عِنْده. It is not good to make ذَا and من a single noun as they were with مَا, because مَا is vague and ذَا was added to it because it is vague like it, whereas من is not like that in vagueness.
His saying {قرضا}: a noun standing for the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar). His saying فيضاعفه لَهُ: whoever reads it in the nominative conjoins it to what is in the ṣila (relative clause), namely يقْرض; and it is also permissible to read it in the nominative as cut off (qaṭʿ) from what precedes. Whoever reads it in the accusative takes it as conjunction with the fāʾ according to the meaning rather than the wording, and so puts it in the accusative. The reasoning for his accusative is that he took it according to the meaning and implied أَن after the fāʾ, so that together with the verb it would be a maṣdar, and you conjoin a maṣdar to a maṣdar; when you imply أَن you put the verb in the accusative. The meaning of his taking it according to the meaning is that the sense of "who is it that will lend Allah a loan" is "whoever has a loan from him, multiples will follow it"; since the meaning of the beginning of the speech is the maṣdar, the second, conjoined by the fāʾ, was made a maṣdar so as to conjoin a maṣdar to a maṣdar; so he needed to imply أَن, so that together with the verb it would be a maṣdar, and he put the verb in the accusative. Thus the fāʾ is a conjunction of sequence, according to its original use in the chapter of conjunction.
It is not good, in the reading of whoever reads the accusative, to make فيضاعفه a response to the interrogative with the fāʾ, because the loan is not what is being asked about; the question is only about the doer of the loan. Do you not see that if you said "Is it Zayd who lends me, so that I thank him (أَزِيد يقرضني فأشكره)?", the accusative as a response to the interrogative would not be permissible, though it would be permissible by taking it according to the meaning, as has passed in the explanation of the verse, because the question did not fall on the lending; it fell only on Zayd. If you said "Will Zayd lend me, so that I thank him (أيقرضني زيد فاشكره)?", the accusative as a response to the interrogative would be permissible, because the question fell on the lending. It was said that the accusative in the verse is as a response to the interrogative, taken according to the meaning, because "who lends Allah" and "who is it that lends Allah" are the same in meaning. The first view is the one held by the people of verification, reflection and analogy.

mekki-muskil:8-8.t:
His words {وَمن النَّاس}: the nūn of من was given fatḥa because it meets a vowelless letter, namely the lām of definiteness, and fatḥa was more fitting for it than kasra because of the kasra of the mīm and frequent usage. The original form of النَّاس according to Sībawayh is الأناس; then the hamza was dropped as it was dropped in الاه, and the lām of definiteness entered. It is also said that its original form is rather نَاس, because the Arabs say نويس in the diminutive. Al-Kisāʾī said: they are two dialectal forms.

His words {من يَقُول}: من is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate). يَقُول has the pattern يفعل and its original form is يَقُول [Translator's note: as written; the original form intended is يَقْوُل], then the vowel of the wāw was cast onto the qāf because it had been weakened in قَالَ. I only mention to you one example of each kind so that you may measure against it whatever comes of its like, since it is not possible to mention everything that occurs of it, out of aversion to repetition and prolixity. Had the speech been «وَمن النَّاس من يَقُولُونَ», it would have been permissible to construe it according to the meaning, as He, Exalted is His mention, said: «وَمِنْهُم من يَسْتَمِعُون إِلَيْك».

The madda in آمن is originally a vowelless hamza; its original form is أأمن, then the vowelless hamza was replaced with alif because of the fatḥa before it. The madda in الآخر is an augment alif for the فَاعل pattern, and its origin is not a hamza.

His words {وَمَا هم بمؤمنين}: هم is the noun (ism) of مَا and مؤمنين is the khabar; the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). According to the Basrans it entered to emphasise the negation; according to the Kufans it entered as an answer to someone who said «إِن زيدا لمنطلق» (Zayd is indeed departing), so مَا corresponds to إِن and the bāʾ corresponds to the lām, since the lām is for emphasising the affirmation and the bāʾ for emphasising the negation.

mekki-muskil:246-246.t:
His saying {نُقَاتِل}: jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request. If it were nominative in ordinary speech it would be permissible, in the sense of "and we will fight". As for what is reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Abī ʿAbla, that they both read it with yāʾ (يقاتل), the better in it is the nominative, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of ملك, and that is how they both read it; if it were jussive as the response it would be permissible. So the jussive with nūn is better and the nominative is permissible; and the nominative with yāʾ is better and the jussive is permissible.
His saying {أَلا تقاتلوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as the khabar (predicate) of عَسى. It and what follows it are a maṣdar (verbal noun) which it is not good to pronounce (explicitly) after عَسى, because the maṣdar does not indicate a definite time, while عَسى requires that it be followed by a future (imperfect) form; and عَسى is not used except with أَن, except in poetry.
His saying وَمَا لنا أَن لَا: أَن is in the position of the accusative on the dropping of the genitive-governing particle [Translator's note: i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition]; its implied form is "and what is with us in (فِي) that we should not fight". Al-Akhfash said أَن is redundant (zāʾida).

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His words {يخادعون الله} may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from من, in which case one does not pause before it; or it may have no position in i'rab, in which case one pauses before it.

mekki-muskil:247-247.t: His saying {طالوت ملكا}: ملكا is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from طالوت.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t:
His words {فِي قُلُوبهم مرض} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and likewise وَلَهُم عَذَاب. أَلِيم is a naʿt (adjective) of العذاب; it is a فعيل with the meaning of مفعول, i.e. مؤلم (painful).

His words {بِمَا كَانُوا}: the bāʾ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the notion of being settled (istiqrār), i.e. "and a painful punishment is settled for them because of their denying what their Prophet brought". مَا with the verb is a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar), and يكذبُون is the khabar of كَانَ.

mekki-muskil:248-248.t: His saying {فِيهِ سكينَة من ربكُم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from التابوت; and likewise تحمله الْمَلَائِكَة is also in the position of a ḥāl from it.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His words {وَإِذا قيل لَهُم}: إِذا is an adverb (ẓarf). Among the grammarians are those who allowed that the operator on it be قيل, and among them are those who disallowed it and assumed an implied verb, indicated by the speech, that governs إِذا; the same is the analogy for whatever is like it. It is also permitted that the operator be قَالُوا, which is the answer to إِذا.

قيل: it is said that its original form is قول on the pattern فعل [i.e. quwila]; then the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the qāf, and the wāw turned into yāʾ because it was vowelless and the letter before it had kasra. There are dialectal variants in it: giving the qāf a tinge (ishmām) of ḍamma; and among them are those who pronounce ḍamma according to its origin, so the wāw remains as it is; and the same is the analogy for whatever resembles it. Al-Akhfash allowed قيل with yāʾ and ḍamma on the qāf; this is anomalous (shādhdh) and has no analogical basis. Ibn Kaysān used to call ishmām "ishāra" (pointing), and it is not heard; and he used to call rawm "ishmām", and it is heard as a faint sound. لَهُم is in the position of the nominative as the deputy agent (mafʿūl lam yusamma fāʿiluhu) of قيل.

His words {نَحن مصلحون} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). The مَا in إِنَّمَا is a restraining (kāffa) mā that restrains إِن from governing. نَحن is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun used for two, for a group, for those speaking of themselves, and for the single exalted person. The nūn of نَحن was given ḍamma rather than kasra or fatḥa because it is a pronoun used for the plural, and the wāw is one of the signs of the plural, and ḍamma is the sister of the wāw, so ḍamma was more fitting for it. It is also said that it is like قبل and بعد, since it indicates speaking of two and of more. It is also said that it is like حَيْثُ, needing two things, so it was strengthened with ḍamma, since it is the strongest of the vowels. It is also said that it is one of the signs of the nominative, so it was given the vowel that resembles the nominative, namely ḍamma. And it is said that its original form is نَحُن with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ, and the vowel of the ḥāʾ was transferred to the nūn.

mekki-muskil:249-249.t:
His saying {إِلَّا من اغترف}: من is in the position of the accusative as excepted from the pronoun in يطعمهُ.
His saying {كم من فِئَة}: كم is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); it is the declarative (khabariyya) kind, and غلبت is its khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t:
His words {أَلا إِنَّهُم}: إِن was given kasra because speech begins with it; it is permitted to give it fatḥa if you make أَلا mean "truly" (ḥaqqan).

His words {هم المفسدون} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the khabar of إِن. It is also permitted that هم be a separating pronoun (fāṣila) with no position in i'rab, or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ and mīm in إِنَّهُم, with المفسدون as the khabar.

mekki-muskil:251-251.t: His saying بِبَعْض: in the position of the object, like «مَرَرْت زيد» [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably «مررت بزيد», "I passed by Zayd"].

mekki-muskil:13-13.t: His words {كَمَا آمن}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "قَالُوا أتؤمن إِيمَانًا مثل مَا آمن السُّفَهَاء" (they said: will you believe with a belief like that with which the fools believed). The first kāf is likewise.

mekki-muskil:252-252.t:
His saying {تِلْكَ}: a vague noun (demonstrative); the tāʾ is the noun, the lām entered to indicate the remoteness of what is pointed to, and the kāf is for address and has no position in i'rab. The origin of تِلْكَ is تيلك: when two kasras came in succession with a yāʾ between them, the lām was made quiescent for lightness, and the yāʾ was dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām. The origin of the lām is fatḥa, because it is a lām of emphasis, but it was given kasra in this to distinguish between it and the lām of possession, when you say تي لَك, i.e. "this is yours". It has been said that the lām entered only to separate the vague noun from the kāf, lest it be thought that it is annexed to the kāf; on this view its origin is sukūn, because it is a particle of meaning; then the yāʾ was dropped because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the lām. The noun according to the Kufans is the tāʾ and the yāʾ, as they said regarding ذَلِك (that the noun is) the dhāl and the alif; the Basrans said the noun is the dhāl. Whoever holds this view about the lām is bound not to allow its omission, [Translator's note: yet] it is permissible according to everyone: you say تيك آيَات الله.
His saying {نتلوها عَلَيْك}: in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from آيَات الله.

mekki-muskil:15-15.t: His words {يعمهون} are a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the accusative pronoun in يمدهُمْ.

mekki-muskil:253-253.t:
His saying {مِنْهُم من كلم الله}: من is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مِنْهُم is the khabar (predicate), and the hāʾ is omitted from كلم, i.e. كَلمه.
His saying {دَرَجَات}: i.e. "to (إِلَى) degrees"; when إِلَى was dropped it was put in the accusative.
His saying {تِلْكَ الرُّسُل}: a mubtadaʾ; الرسل is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and فضلنا and what follows it is the khabar.

mekki-muskil:254-254.t: His saying {لَا بيع فِيهِ وَلَا خلة وَلَا شَفَاعَة}: all these sentences are in the position of a repeated naʿt (adjective) of يَوْم. The fatḥa and the nominative in this are like فَلَا رفث وَلَا فسوق, since its origin is all mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and the sentence is in the position of the naʿt of يَوْم.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His words {اشْتَروا الضَّلَالَة}: its original form is اشتريوا. The yāʾ was turned into alif; it is also said that it was made vowelless for lightness, but the first is better and more in keeping with the principles. Then, on both views, it was dropped because it was vowelless and the wāw of the plural after it was vowelless. The wāw in اشْتَروا was given a vowel because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and ḍamma was chosen for it to distinguish the wāw of the plural from the radical wāw, as in لَو استقاموا [Translator's note: as written; the usual example of a radical wāw is «لَوِ اسْتَطَعْنَا», and the wāw of استقاموا is itself a plural wāw]. Al-Farrāʾ said: it was given the same vowel as the dropped yāʾ before it. Ibn Kaysān said: ḍamma on the wāw is lighter than kasra, so it was chosen, since it is of its own kind. Al-Zajjāj said: ḍamma was chosen for it because it is the wāw of the plural, so it was given ḍamma just as the nūn in نَحن was given ḍamma, since that too is plural. It has been read with kasra according to the original rule, and al-Kisāʾī allowed pronouncing it with hamza because of its ḍamma, though that is far-fetched. It has also been read with fatḥa on the wāw for lightness.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t:
His words {أَضَاءَت مَا حوله}: مَا is in the position of the accusative by أَضَاءَت, and النَّار is the fāʿil (agent), latent (muḍmar) in أَضَاءَت. The answer of فَلَمَّا is omitted, its implied form being "فَلَمَّا أَضَاءَت مَا حوله طفئت" (when it lit up what was around him, it was extinguished).

His words {لَا يبصرون} are in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ and mīm in تَركهم. His words صم are nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), and likewise what follows it. It is permitted to put all of that in the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in تَركهم, which is the reading of Ibn Masʿūd and Ḥafṣa; and it is permitted to put it in the accusative by an implied أَعنِي (I mean).

His words {ذهب}: ذهب [with bāʾ] and أذهب have the same meaning, but the bāʾ is dropped when the hamza enters.

mekki-muskil:18-18.t: His words {فهم لَا يرجعُونَ} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), likewise in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تَركهم.

mekki-muskil:19-19.t:
His words {كصيب}: its original form is صيوب on the pattern فيعل; then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ. Lightening the yāʾ (pronouncing it without doubling) is permitted. The Kufans said: it is فعيل, originally صويب, then assimilated; but they would then be obliged to assimilate in طَوِيل and عويل, and that is not permitted.

His words {فِيهِ ظلمات} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a khabar (predicate) placed first, and the clause is in the position of the naʿt (adjective) of الصيب. The kāf of كصيب is in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the kāf in His words كَمثل الَّذِي; or it is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of His words مثلهم, its implied form being "مثلهم مثل الَّذِي استوقد نَارا أَو مثل صيب" (their likeness is the likeness of one who kindled a fire, or the likeness of a rainstorm). If you wish, you may imply a mubtadaʾ of which the kāf is the khabar, its implied form being "أَو مثلهم مثل صيب" (or their likeness is the likeness of a rainstorm).

His words {يجْعَلُونَ} are in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تَركهم, i.e. "He left them in darkness, not seeing, not understanding, putting their fingers…". If you wish, you may make these ḥāl clauses cut off from what precedes and resumptive, in which case they have no position in i'rab. It has also been said that يجْعَلُونَ is a ḥāl from the pronoun in فِيهِ, which refers to الصيب, as though He said "putting their fingers in their ears because of its thunderbolts", meaning those of the rainstorm.

His words {حذر الْمَوْت} are a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

His words {وَالله مُحِيط} are a mubtadaʾ and khabar. The original form of مُحِيط is محوط; the kasra of the wāw was transferred to the ḥāʾ, and the wāw turned into yāʾ because it was vowelless and the letter before it had kasra.

mekki-muskil:20-20.t:
His words {يكَاد الْبَرْق}: يكَاد is a verb of approximation. When there is no negation with it, [the action] came close to happening but did not happen, as here. When negation accompanies it, it happened after delay, as in His words «فذبحوها وَمَا كَادُوا يَفْعَلُونَ», i.e. they carried out the slaughter after delay. The original form of كَاد, the one of approximation, is كود, and of يكَاد, يكود; the wāw was turned into alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, as in خَاف يخَاف.

His words {كلما} are accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) by مَشوا. When كلما is an adverb, the operator on it is the verb that is its answer, namely مَشوا, because it contains the meaning of a condition, so it needs an answer. أَضَاء does not govern it, because it is within the ṣila (relative clause) of مَا. Similarly with «كلما رزقوا», the answer is قَالُوا, and it is the operator on كل. مَا is an incomplete noun whose ṣila is the verb that follows it, and كلما contains the meaning of a condition.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His words {يَا أَيهَا النَّاس}: أي is a singular vocative (munādā mufrad) with ḍamma, and النَّاس is a naʿt (adjective) of it. According to most grammarians it is not permitted to put النَّاس in the accusative, because it is a naʿt that may not be omitted, so it is the one addressed in meaning, as though He said "يَا نَاس" (O people). Al-Māzinī allowed its accusative according to the position, just as «يَا زيد الظريف» (O Zayd, the witty one) is permitted [with the accusative] according to the position.

His words {تَتَّقُون}: its original form is توتقيون. The wāw was assimilated into the tāʾ after being turned into tāʾ; the vowel of the yāʾ was cast onto the qāf, and the yāʾ was dropped because it was vowelless and the wāw of the plural after it was vowelless. It is تفتعلون, and likewise its like wherever it occurs.

mekki-muskil:22-22.t:
His words {الَّذِي جعل لكم}: الَّذِي is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ربكم, or of الَّذِي, or as the object of تَتَّقُون, or by an implied أَعنِي (I mean); or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ with the khabar (predicate) implied.

His words {وَأَنْتُم تعلمُونَ} are a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تجْعَلُوا.

mekki-muskil:255-255.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, {الله لَا إِلَه إِلَّا هُوَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and هُوَ is a badal (substitute) from the position of لَا إِلَه. Its precise analysis is that الله is a mubtadaʾ, لا إله is a second mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "Allah: there is no god worshipped except He"; إلا هو is a badal from the position of لا إله, and the sentence is the khabar about الله. Likewise your saying لَا إِلَه إِلَّا الله: (لا إله) is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, and إلا الله is a badal from the position of لا إله and a description of it according to the position. If you wish, you may make إلا الله the khabar of لا إله. The accusative as an exception is also permissible.
His saying {القيوم}: it is of the pattern فيعول from قَامَ, and its origin is قيووم; when the yāʾ preceded the wāw and the first was quiescent, the wāw was replaced by yāʾ and the yāʾ was assimilated into the yāʾ; reverting to the yāʾ was lighter than the yāʾ reverting to the wāw. It is a naʿt (adjective) of الله, or a khabar after a khabar, or a badal from هُوَ, or nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ; and likewise الْحَيّ. If it were accusative outside the Quran, it would be permissible as praise (madḥ).
His saying {سنة}: its origin is وَسنة; then the wāw was dropped as it was dropped in يسن, and the vowel of the wāw was transferred to the sīn.

mekki-muskil:256-256.t: His saying {لَا انفصام لَهَا}: it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from العروة الوثقى, which is "there is no god but Allah" in the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him.

mekki-muskil:257-257.t: His saying {الطاغوت}: it is a noun used for the singular and the plural, and it is treated as masculine and feminine. It is derived from طَغى, but it is metathesized (maqlūb): its origin is طغيوت on the pattern فعلوت, like جبروت; then the yāʾ was moved into the place of the ghayn and it became طيغوت; then the yāʾ turned into alif because it was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa, and it became طاغوت. So its origin is فعلوت, metathesized to فلعوت. It may also be that the original of its lām (third radical) is wāw, so its origin would be طغووت, because one says طغا يطغو and يطغى, and طغيت and طغوت. Similar to it in metathesis, weakening and pattern is حَانُوت, because it is from حنا يحنو; its origin is حنووت, then it was metathesized and weakened. It cannot be from حَان يحين, because of their saying حوانيت in the plural.

mekki-muskil:258-258.t:
His saying {أَن آتَاهُ الله}: أَن (with its clause) is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
His saying {إِذْ قَالَ}: the governing word (ʿāmil) in إِذْ is تَرَ. The hāʾ in ربه refers back to الَّذِي, who is Nimrod (نمروذ), may Allah curse him; so said Mujāhid.

mekki-muskil:259-259.t:
His saying {أَو كَالَّذي}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, conjoined according to the meaning of the speech; its implied form according to al-Farrāʾ and al-Kisāʾī is "have you seen (one) like the one who disputed with Ibrāhīm, or like the one who passed by a town".
His saying {كم لَبِثت}: كم is in the position of the accusative as a ẓarf (adverb); here it is an adverb of time, by which one asks about the length of the time that ʿUzayr, upon him be peace, remained in his death.
His saying {لم يتسنه}: its meaning may be "its smell has not changed", from their saying تسنى الطَّعَام when its smell or taste changes. Its origin would then be يتسنن on the pattern يتفعل with three nūns; the third was replaced by alif because of the repetition of identical letters, and it became يتسنى; then the alif was dropped for the jussive and يتسن remained; then the hāʾ was brought to make clear the vowel of the nūn in pause. Its meaning may also be "the years have not changed it", in which case the hāʾ in it is radical, the lām (third radical) of the verb, because the origin of سنة is سنهة, and its sukūn is for the jussive; so it is not permissible to drop it either in continuous reading or in pause.

mekki-muskil:260-260.t:
His saying {وَإِذ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيم}: the governing word in إِذْ is an implied verb, its implied form being "and remember, O Muhammad, when Ibrāhīm said".
His saying {كَيفَ تحيي الْمَوْتَى}: كَيفَ is in the position of the accusative, and it is a question about a state; its implied form is "My Lord, show me in what state You give life to the dead".
His saying {لِيَطمَئِن قلبِي}: the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied verb, its implied form being "but I asked You so that my heart may be at rest", or "but show me so that my heart may be at rest".
His saying {على كل جبل مِنْهُنَّ جُزْءا}: i.e. on every mountain a part of each one, and that is greater in (showing) power.
His saying سعيا: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:261-261.t: His saying {مائَة حَبَّة}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is its khabar (predicate). In ordinary speech مائَة in the accusative is permissible, in the sense of "it grew a hundred grains".

mekki-muskil:263-263.t:
His saying {قَول مَعْرُوف}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its naʿt (adjective), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "a kind word is more fitting for you".
His saying {ومغفرة خير من صَدَقَة يتبعهَا أَذَى}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar; يتبعها is a naʿt of الصدقة in the position of the genitive; and أذى is a maqṣūr noun (ending in alif) in which the i'rab does not appear, like هدى, and its position is nominative by its verb (as fāʿil, agent).

mekki-muskil:264-264.t:
His saying {كَالَّذي ينْفق}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a nullifying like the one who…". Likewise رِيَاء is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "a spending of showing off". It is also permissible for رِيَاء to be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it is permissible for it to be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).
His saying {عَلَيْهِ تُرَاب}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the genitive as a naʿt of صَفْوَان.

mekki-muskil:265-265.t:
His saying {أَصَابَهَا وابل}: in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of جنة or of ربوة, as you say "I passed by a slave-girl in a house which Zayd bought".
His saying {ابْتِغَاء مرضات الله وتثبيتا}: both are mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). الصفوان according to al-Kisāʾī is singular, and its plural is صَفْوَان, صفي and صفي [Translator's note: so in the source; the vowelling distinguishing these forms is not given]. It was said it may be plural and singular. It was said that صِفْوان with kasra on the first letter is the plural of صفا, like أخ and إخوان. Al-Akhfash said that صَفْوان with fatḥa is the plural of صفوانة, and He said عَلَيْهِ only because the plural is treated as masculine.

mekki-muskil:266-266.t: His saying {من نخيل وأعناب}: in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of الجنة, and تجري من تحتهَا is a second naʿt; or it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from جنَّة, because it has been described. It is also permissible for it to be the khabar (predicate) of كان.

mekki-muskil:268-268.t: His saying {الشَّيْطَان يَعدكُم}: شَيْطَان is of the pattern فيعال from شطن, (said) when one is far. It cannot be of the pattern فعلان from تشيط and شاط, because Sībawayh reported "شيطنته فتشيطن"; if it were from شاط, then شيطنته would be on the pattern فعلنته, and this form does not exist in the speech of the Arabs. So it is فيعلته, like بيطرته; the nūn is radical and the yāʾ is extra. So the nūn must be the lām (third radical), and شَيْطَان must be فيعال from شطن, when one is far; it is as though, when he was far from the mercy of Allah, he was named with that.

mekki-muskil:270-270.t: His saying {وَمَا أنفقتم} {وَمَا تنفقوا من خير}: مَا in these is in the position of the accusative because the verb after it falls upon it, and it is conditional. As for وَمَا تنفقون, مَا is a negating particle. The hāʾ in His saying فان الله يُعلمهُ refers back to the vow (النذر) or to the spending.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t: His words {أعدت للْكَافِرِينَ} are in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from النَّار. الوقود with fatḥa is the firewood, and with ḍamma it is the maṣdar (verbal noun), namely the kindling; just as الوَضوء with fatḥa is the water, and الوُضوء with ḍamma is the maṣdar, the name for the movements of the one performing ablution.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t:
His words {متشابها} are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in بِهِ.

The hāʾ in His words {من مثله} refers to the Quran; it is also said: to Muḥammad ﷺ.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t:
His words {أَن يضْرب}: أَن is in the position of the accusative; its implied form is "من أَن يضْرب". When من was dropped, the verb, namely يستحي, passed on to it directly and made أَن accusative.

His words {مَا بعوضة}: مَا is redundant (zāʾida) and بعوضة is a badal (substitute) for مثلا. It is also permitted that مَا be in the position of the accusative as an indefinite noun, a badal for مثلا, with بعوضة as a naʿt (adjective) of مَا.

His words {فَمَا فَوْقهَا}: مَا is conjoined to the first مَا, or to بعوضة if you make [the first] مَا redundant. It is permitted to put بعوضة in the nominative by making مَا equivalent to الَّذِي and implying هُوَ, so that بعوضة is its khabar (predicate).

His words {فَأَما الَّذين آمنُوا}: أما is a particle containing the meaning of a condition, and it occurs with the mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar; that is why the fāʾ entered after it. الَّذين is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and فيعلمون and what follows it is the khabar. The second أما is likewise.

His words {مَاذَا أَرَادَ الله}: مَا and ذَا are a single interrogative noun in the position of the accusative by أَرَادَ; its implied form is "which thing did Allah intend by this parable?". If you wish, you may make ذَا mean الَّذِي, so that مَا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ and what follows it is its khabar; أَرَادَ does not govern it then, because it is in the ṣila (relative clause) of الَّذِي, and the ṣila does not govern what precedes the relative, nor the relative itself. So ذَا with its ṣila is in the position of the nominative as the khabar of مَا, and with أَرَادَ there is an omitted hāʾ referring to الَّذِي; its implied form is "what is it that Allah intended by this parable?". مثلا is accusative as tafsīr (specification, i.e. tamyīz); it is also said that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from ذَا in هَذَا, the operator on it being the pointing and the drawing of attention.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t:
His words {أَن يُوصل}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for مَا. It is also said that أَن is accusative in the sense of "لِئَلَّا يُوصل" (so that it not be joined). Or, if you wish, it is in the position of the genitive as a badal for the hāʾ in بِهِ, and this is the best of them.

His words {ميثاقه}: it is a noun in the position of the maṣdar (verbal noun), because it means إيثاقه (His binding it).

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His words {كَيفَ تكفرون}: كَيفَ is in the position of the accusative by تكفرون. The hāʾ in His words ثمَّ إِلَيْهِ ترجعون refers to Allah, Exalted is His mention; it is also said that it rather refers to the bringing to life (al-iḥyāʾ).

mekki-muskil:29-29.t:
His words {جَمِيعًا} are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from مَا, and the operator on it is خلق.

His words {فسواهن سبع سماوات}: سبع is a badal (substitute) for the hāʾ and nūn. It is also said that it is the object of سوى, its implied form being "فسوى مِنْهُنَّ سبع سماوات" (He made of them seven heavens); so the preposition is omitted together with the hāʾ and nūn, just as He said «وَاخْتَارَ مُوسَى قومه», i.e. من قومه (from his people); then the preposition was dropped and what follows it became accusative.

The pronoun only refers in the plural form to السَّمَاء, whose form is singular, because it is the plural of سماوة and سماءة, like تمرة and تمر; it is a plural distinguished from its singular by the hāʾ. When the hāʾ was dropped in the plural, the wāw turned into hamza, as they turned it in الدُّعَاء and الكساء, the origin of whose hamza is wāw because they are from دَعَا يَدْعُو and كسا يكسو.

mekki-muskil:30-30.t:
His words {وَإِذ قَالَ رَبك}: إِذْ is in the position of the accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "وَاذْكُر يَا مُحَمَّد إِذْ قَالَ" (and remember, O Muḥammad, when He said). قَالَ does not govern it, because إِذْ is muḍāf (in genitive construct) to the clause after it, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf.

His words {أَتجْعَلُ فِيهَا}: the alif is the alif of seeking guidance, a question about the benefit, not a disapproval; its form is the form of the interrogative. It is also said that it is wonder: the angels wondered at the power of Allah.

His words {إِنِّي أعلم}: it is good for أعلم to be a verb of one speaking of himself, because before it there is speech about oneself, namely إِنِّي. It may also be a noun in the sense of an active participle (fāʿil), in which case tanwīn is assumed in it — but it is diptote — so it makes مَا accusative.

His words {للْمَلَائكَة}: it is the plural of ملك. The original form of ملك is مألك; then the hamza was transposed and put back in the position of the lām, so it became ملأك. Its original pattern is مفعل, transposed to معفل. Then the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the lām, so it became ملك. When it was put into the plural it was returned to its original after the transposition; that is why the hamza comes after the lām in مَلَائِكَة. Had it been pluralised on its original before the transposition, you would have said مآلكة on the pattern مفاعلة. So مَلَائِكَة has the pattern معافلة and its origin is مفاعلة: the hamza is the fāʾ (first radical) of the word in its origin, the lām is the ʿayn (second radical) and the kāf is the lām (third radical), because it is derived from الألوكة, which is the message.

Ibn Kaysān said: it is derived from ملكت, and the hamza is an augment according to him, like its augmentation in شمأل; so the pattern of ملك is فعل and the pattern of مَلَائِكَة is فعائلة, because the mīm is radical and the hamza is an augment. Abū ʿUbayd said: it is derived from لأك when one sends; so the hamza is the ʿayn, and there is no transposition in it on Abū ʿUbayd's view.

So the pattern of the word مَلَائِكَة on the view of the majority is معافلة, because it is transposed and the hamza is the fāʾ of the word; on the view of Ibn Kaysān it is فعائلة, because the mīm is radical and the hamza is an augment according to him; and on the view of Abū ʿUbayd it is مفاعلة, because the hamza according to him is the ʿayn of the word.

mekki-muskil:32-32.t:
His words {سُبْحَانَكَ} are accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun). Tasbīḥ is the declaring of Allah free of evil (tanzīh); so it stands for "نسبحك تسبيحا" (we glorify You with glorification), i.e. "we declare You free of evil, with a declaring free, and we absolve You of it".

His words {إِنَّك أَنْت}: if you wish, you may make أَنْت in the position of the accusative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the kāf. If you wish, you may make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with الْعَلِيم as its khabar (predicate), it and its khabar being the khabar of إِن. If you wish, you may make it a separating pronoun (fāṣila) with no position in i'rab. الْحَكِيم is a naʿt (adjective) of الْعَلِيم, or, if you wish, you may make it a khabar after a khabar of إِن.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His words {وَأعلم مَا تبدون}: أعلم may be a verb, as was what preceded it, so مَا is in the position of the accusative by it. It may also be a noun in the sense of عَالم (knower), so that مَا is in the position of the genitive by أعلم being made muḍāf (genitive construct) to it, as the active participle is made muḍāf. It is also permitted to assume tanwīn in the active participle — but it is diptote — so that مَا is in the position of the accusative, just as you say «هَؤُلَاءِ حواج بَيت الله» (these are pilgrims to the House of Allah), putting بَيت in the accusative by assuming tanwīn in حواج.

mekki-muskil:34-34.t:
His words {وَإِذ قُلْنَا} are like وَإِذ قَالَ.

His words {إِلَّا إِبْلِيس}: إِبْلِيس is accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It is diptote because it is foreign and definite. Abū ʿUbayd said: it is Arabic, derived from أبلس, said when one despairs of good, but it has no counterpart among the nouns, and it is definite, so it is diptote for that reason.

The hāʾ in خَليفَة and مَلَائِكَة is for intensification; it is also said: for the feminine of the form. خَليفَة is فعيلة in the sense of فاعلة, i.e. they succeed one another.

آدَم is أفعل, derived from الأدمة, which is the colour [brownness]; so it is diptote because it is definite, its origin is an adjective, and it is on the pattern of the verb. It is also said that it is derived from أَدِيم الأَرْض, which is its surface; but this is far-fetched, because its pattern could then be فَاعِل, like طابق, and it would have to be declinable, since there is nothing of the meaning of an adjective in it, and أفعل originally is an adjective.

mekki-muskil:35-35.t: His words {رغدا} are a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "أكلا رغدا" (an eating in abundance); and it — I mean the omitted maṣdar — is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) according to Ibn Kaysān. The nūn was dropped from فتكونا because it is accusative as the answer to the prohibition; it is also permitted that the dropping of the nūn be for the jussive, in which case it is conjoined to وَلَا تقربا.

mekki-muskil:36-36.t: His words {بَعْضكُم لبَعض عَدو} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), cut off from what precedes. Or, if you wish, in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in اهبطوا. In the speech a wāw is omitted, and it was dispensed with because of the pronoun that refers back to the pronoun in اهبطوا; its implied form is "قُلْنَا اهبطوا وبعضكم لبَعض عَدو", i.e. "go down, and this is your state". Retaining it in speech is good. If there were no resumptive pronoun in the speech, dropping the wāw would not be permitted: if you said «لقيتك وَزيد رَاكب» (I met you while Zayd was riding), dropping the wāw would not be permitted; but if you said «رَاكب إِلَيْك» (riding towards you), both dropping and retaining the wāw would be permitted.

mekki-muskil:37-37.t: His words {إِنَّه هُوَ التواب الرَّحِيم}: هُوَ, in its various analyses, is equivalent to أَنْت in إِنَّك أَنْت الْعَلِيم الْحَكِيم.

mekki-muskil:38-38.t:
His words جَمِيعًا are a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in اهبطوا.

His words {فإمَّا يَأْتينكُمْ}: إمّا is a conditional particle that makes verbs jussive; it is the conditional إِن with which مَا has been added for emphasis, and the doubled nūn has also entered for emphasis; but the verb with the nūn is indeclinable (mabnī), not declined.

His words {هدى} are in the position of the nominative by its verb; its origin has already been mentioned.

His words {فَمن تبع هُدَايَ}: من is a complete conditional noun, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); it makes jussive the future verbs that follow it and its answer. A past verb after it is in the position of the jussive; neither من nor any other conditional particle changes it [in form], rather they change its meaning, so that its meaning becomes future while its form does not change.

mekki-muskil:271-271.t:
His saying {فَنعما هِيَ}: in نعم there are four dialectal forms: نَعِم, like عَلِم; نِعِم, with kasra on the nūn following the kasra of the ʿayn, because it is a guttural letter whose preceding letter follows it in vowel in most dialects; نَعْم, leaving the nūn with fatḥa as in its origin and making the ʿayn quiescent for lightness; and نِعْم, with kasra on the nūn because of the kasra of the ʿayn, then the ʿayn is made quiescent for lightness. Whoever of the readers gives kasra to the nūn and the ʿayn, it is possible that the kasra of the ʿayn is according to the dialect of those who give it kasra and make the nūn follow it; and it is possible that it is according to the dialect of those who make the ʿayn quiescent and give kasra to the nūn, but he gave the ʿayn kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. As for making the ʿayn quiescent together with the assimilation, that is impossible: it is not permissible and not possible in pronunciation. Whoever gives fatḥa to the nūn and kasra to the ʿayn may have read according to the dialect of those who say نَعِم like عَلِم; and it may be that he made the ʿayn quiescent for lightness, and when it was joined to the assimilated letter he gave it kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
مَا is in the position of the accusative as tafsīr (specification). In نعم there is a pronoun, nominative by نعم, and it is the pronoun of the alms (الصَّدقَات); هِيَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate); its implied form is "if you disclose the alms, then they are — excellent a thing (نعم شَيْئا)".
His saying {وَيكفر عَنْكُم من سَيِّئَاتكُمْ}: whoever reads it in the jussive conjoins it to the position of the fāʾ in His saying فَهُوَ خير لكم; and whoever reads it in the nominative does so as cut off (qaṭʿ). Whoever reads it with nūn and in the nominative takes its implied form as "and We shall remove"; and whoever reads it with yāʾ and in the nominative takes its implied form as "and Allah will remove from you".

mekki-muskil:272-272.t: His saying {وَأَنْتُم لَا تظْلمُونَ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in إِلَيْكُم.

mekki-muskil:273-273.t:
His saying {للْفُقَرَاء}: the lām is attached to (mutaʿalliq) something omitted, its implied form being "give to the poor".
His saying {لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ ضربا فِي الأَرْض}: in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in أحْصرُوا. يحسبهم is also a ḥāl from الْفُقَرَاء, and likewise تعرفهم, and likewise لَا يسْأَلُون النَّاس إلحافا; and it is good for that to be a ḥāl from the pronoun in احصروا. It is possible that all of that is cut off from what precedes it, having no grammatical position. And إلحافا is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl.

mekki-muskil:274-274.t:
His saying {سرا وَعَلَانِيَة}: two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun in يُنْفقُونَ.
His saying {الَّذين يُنْفقُونَ أَمْوَالهم}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
His saying {فَلهم أجرهم}: also a mubtadaʾ and khabar. The fāʾ entered because of the vagueness in الَّذين: by its vagueness it resembled the vagueness in the condition, so the fāʾ entered its khabar by resemblance to the condition. الَّذِي resembles the condition only when there is a verb in its ṣila (relative clause), as in "whoever comes to me, then he has a dirham (الَّذِي يأتيني فَلهُ دِرْهَم)". If you said "the one in whose house Zayd is, then he has a dirham (الَّذِي زيد فِي دَاره فَلهُ دِرْهَم)", the entry of the fāʾ into its khabar would be ugly, since there is no verb in its ṣila. And this happens with الَّذِي only when no governing word that changes its meaning has entered upon it; if a governing word that changes its meaning enters upon it, the entry of the fāʾ into its khabar is not permissible, as in لَعَلَّ الَّذِي يقوم زيد and ليت الَّذِي يحرج عَمْرو [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably يخرج]: the entry of the fāʾ into its khabar is not permissible, because its meaning is changed by what has entered upon it. So understand it.

mekki-muskil:275-275.t:
His saying {الَّذين يَأْكُلُون}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is لَا يقومُونَ and what follows it.
His saying {فَمن جَاءَهُ موعظة}: He made جَاءَ masculine, taking it according to the meaning, because it is in the sense of "whoever an admonition (وعظ) comes to". It was said it is masculine because the femininity of الموعظة is not real, since it has no masculine from its own wording. It was said it is masculine because there is a separation between the verb of the feminine and it, by the hāʾ.
His saying {الرِّبَا}: it is from wāw, and its dual is ربوان according to Sībawayh, and it is written with alif. The Kufans said it is written with yāʾ and made dual with yāʾ because of the kasra at its beginning; and likewise they say regarding triliteral nouns with wāw (as third radical) when the first letter has kasra or ḍamma, as in رَبًّا [Translator's note: so in the source] and ضحى; if the first letter has fatḥa, they write it with alif and make it dual with wāw, as the Basrans said, as in صفا.

mekki-muskil:280-280.t:
His saying {وَإِن كَانَ ذُو عسرة}: كَانَ is complete (tāmma), not needing a khabar (predicate); its implied form is "and if one in hardship occurs", and it is general to all people. If you put ذا in the accusative as the khabar of كَانَ, it would become specific to particular people; for this reason the well-known readers are unanimous on the nominative of ذُو. As for His saying أَن تكون تِجَارَة: whoever reads تِجَارَة in the nominative makes كَانَ in the sense of "occur" and "happen", and تديرونها is a naʿt (adjective) of التجارة; it was also said it is the khabar of كَانَ. Whoever reads تِجَارَة in the accusative implies the noun (ism) of كَانَ in it, its implied form being "except that the trade is a trade circulated among you". And أَن in إِلَّا أَن is in the position of the accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).
His saying {فنظرة إِلَى ميسرَة}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar, and it (نظرة) is from (the sense of) delaying. Whoever reads ميسرَة with annexation (to the pronoun), that is far-fetched, since there is no مفعُل in the language; as for مفعُلة, it has come in the language, though it is rare, and no one but Nāfiʿ read with it; whereas مفعَل and مفعَلة are common in the language [Translator's note: the source does not mark the vowel of the ʿayn in these patterns; the contrast is presumably between maf'ul(a) with ḍamma and the common forms].
His saying {وَأَن تصدقوا}: أَن is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and خير is its khabar.

mekki-muskil:281-281.t: His saying {ترجعون فِيهِ}: in the position of the accusative, a naʿt (adjective) of يَوْم.

mekki-muskil:282-282.t:
His saying {فَرجل وَامْرَأَتَانِ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "then a man and two women take the place of the two men". In يَكُونَا there is the pronoun of the two witnesses, and it is the noun (ism) of كان, and رجلين is its khabar. It was said the implied form is "then a man and two women bear witness", and this omitted khabar is what governs أَن تضل. His saying أَن تضل: the position of أَن is accusative, and what governs it is the omitted khabar, namely يشْهدُونَ, on the implied form "because (لِأَن)", as you say "I prepared the plank in case the wall tilts, so that I prop it up (أَعدَدْت الْخَشَبَة ليميل الْحَائِط فأدعمه)"; and it is like the poet's saying:
... فللموت مَا تَلد الوالده ...
(So for death is what the mother bears.)
So he reported the outcome of the matter and its cause. Whoever reads إن with kasra makes it a condition, and the position of the condition and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is nominative, because it is a naʿt (adjective) of امرأتين.
His saying {مِمَّن ترْضونَ من الشُّهَدَاء}: in the position of the nominative, a description of رجل and امرأتين. His saying شهيدين does not enter with them in the description, because of the difference in i'rab between the two described nouns. It is not good for استشهدوا to govern أَن تضل, because they were not commanded to take witnesses in order that one of the two women should err.
His saying {أَلا ترتابوا}: أَن is in the position of the accusative; its implied form is "and nearer to (من) your not doubting".
His saying {إِلَّا أَن تكون}: in the position of the accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ).
His saying {أَلا تكتبوها}: أَن is in the position of the accusative; its implied form is "then there is no blame on you in (فِي) not writing it".
His saying {وَلَا يضار كَاتب وَلَا شَهِيد}: it is permissible for the two to be agents (fāʿil), with يضار being يفاعل; and it is permissible for them to be objects whose agent is not named [Translator's note: i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)], with يضار being يفاعل; and the better is for it to be يفاعل [Translator's note: the source does not vowel these patterns; presumably the first is the active يُفاعِل, the second the passive يُفاعَل, and the preferred one the active], because after it comes وان تَفعلُوا فَإِنَّهُ فسوق بكم, addressing the witnesses. The hāʾ in وليه refers back to the debt; it was said it refers back to the owner of the debt, who is the orphan and the incapable; and it was said it refers back to the one from whom (payment) is sought.

mekki-muskil:39-39.t:
His words {وهم فِيهَا خَالدُونَ} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from أَصْحَاب or from النَّار, just as you say «زيد ملك الدَّار وَهُوَ جَالس فِيهَا» (Zayd owned the house while sitting in it): your words وَهُوَ جَالس are a ḥāl from the pronoun in ملك, i.e. he owned it in the state of his sitting in it. If you wish, you may make it a ḥāl from الدَّار, because in the clause there are two pronouns, one referring to Zayd and the other referring to the house, so the ḥāl from both of them is good because of the pronoun. Had you said «زيد ملك الدَّار وَهُوَ جَالس», it could only be a ḥāl from the pronoun in ملك and nothing else, since there is no pronoun in the clause referring to the house. Had you said «زيد ملك الدَّار وَهِي مَبْنِيَّة» (Zayd owned the house while it was built), the clause could only be in the position of the ḥāl from the house, since there is no pronoun referring to the pronoun in ملك; but if you added «من مَاله» (from his wealth) or the like, it could be a ḥāl from the pronoun and from the house. Likewise the verse: since in His words هم فِيهَا خَالدُونَ there are two pronouns, it may be a ḥāl from both of them. So measure against these two whatever resembles them, for this is a principle that recurs often in the Quran.

Some grammarians disallowed the ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi: had you said «رَأَيْت غُلَام هِنْد قَائِمَة» (I saw Hind's servant, she standing), it would not be permitted according to him, since there is no operator to govern the ḥāl. Some of them allowed it, because the lām of possession is implied with the muḍāf ilayhi, so the meaning of possession is the operator on the ḥāl, or the meaning of attachment (mulāzama), or the meaning of accompaniment (muṣāḥaba). On the view of those who disallow the ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi, هم فِيهَا خَالدُونَ cannot be a ḥāl from النَّار. Analogous to it is أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَاب الْجنَّة هم فِيهَا خَالدُونَ.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t:
His words {يَا بني إِسْرَائِيل}: [إِسْرَائِيل] is a definite foreign noun, and that is why it is diptote.
