The causes that prevent nouns from being fully declinable are ten: definiteness; the pattern of the verb; being an adjective; foreignness; the feminine alif, extended and shortened; femininity that has no masculine of its own form; deflection (ʿadl); the two augment letters alif and nūn; two nouns made into a single noun; and a plural pattern that has no counterpart in the singular. When two of these causes combine in a noun it is diptote, and when one occurs alone it is declinable. So make this a principle against which you measure all speech. Some have added to the causes the permanence of a single cause.

His words {وأوفوا}: its original form is أوفيوا; the vowel of the yāʾ was moved back onto the fāʾ, and the yāʾ was dropped because it was vowelless and the wāw after it was vowelless.

His words {أوف بعهدكم} are jussive because it is the answer to the imperative.

His words {وإياي فارهبون}: إيَّايَ is accusative by an implied verb; this is preferred because it is a command. «وَأَنا فارهبون» is permitted as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); this is equivalent to your saying «زيد فَاضْرِبْهُ» (Zayd — strike him), because the yāʾ dropped from فارهبون is like the hāʾ in اضربه. But the verb that makes إيَّايَ accusative is implied after it, its implied form being "وإياي ارهبوا فارهبون" (and Me fear, so fear Me); had you implied it before it, it would become attached to it, and you would say «وارهبوني فارهبون».

mekki-muskil:41-41.t:
His words {مُصدقا} are a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ dropped from أنزلت, its implied form being أنزلته, because مَا means الَّذِي. If you wish, you may make it a ḥāl from مَا in بِمَا.

His words {أول كَافِر}: أول is a noun from which no verb is pronounced, according to Sībawayh. Its pattern is أفعل; its fāʾ (first radical) is wāw and its ʿayn (second radical) is wāw, and that is why no verb is used from it, because of the combination of wāws.

The Kufans said: it is أفعل from وأل, said when one escapes, so its original form is أوأل; then the second hamza was lightened by replacing it with wāw and assimilating the first [wāw] into it, just as they said مقروة in lightening مقروءة. They treated the radical letter like the augment in مقروءة. It would have been better, had it been lightened according to the analogical rule, to say أَوَل, casting the vowel of the hamza onto the wāw, as they said ضو in lightening ضوء; and the weakening of the wāw is not obligatory because the vowel is incidental. It is also said that it is أفعل from آل يؤول, its original form being أأول; then it was transposed, the fāʾ being put back in the position of the ʿayn, so it became أوأل with the pattern أعفل; then the same lightening, replacement and assimilation were applied to it as in the first view. So its pattern after the transposition is أفعل [Translator's note: as written; by the author's own account the pattern after transposition would be أعفل]. The discussion of أولى is like the discussion of أول in both views, since it is the feminine of أول.

أول is accusative as the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ. كَافِر is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted noun, its implied form being "أول فريق كَافِر" (the first party to disbelieve); that is why it came in the singular form while the address is to a group. It is also said that its implied form is "أول من كفر بِهِ" (the first who disbelieves in it).

mekki-muskil:42-42.t:
His words {وتكتموا الْحق}: تكتموا is accusative because it is the answer to the prohibition; the dropping of the nūn is the sign of the accusative and the jussive in it and in whatever is like it. It may also be jussive, conjoined to تلبسوا.

His words {وَأَنْتُم تعلمُونَ} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in تكتموا. Likewise وَأَنْتُم تتلون الْكتاب is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the ḥāl from the pronoun in تنسون. The original form of تنسون is تنسيون; the yāʾ was turned into alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, then it was dropped because it was vowelless and the wāw after it was vowelless, and the sīn remained with fatḥa to indicate the dropped alif. The same is the analogy for whatever is like it, of verbs whose imperfect comes on the pattern يفعل with fatḥa on the ʿayn and whose lām (third radical) is yāʾ or wāw, such as يَخْشونَ, يرضون and the like.

mekki-muskil:43-43.t: His words {وَأقِيمُوا}: its pattern is أفعلوا and its original form is أقوموا. The vowel of the wāw was cast onto the qāf, so [the qāf] took kasra, and the wāw turned into yāʾ because of the kasra before it. Its maṣdar (verbal noun) is إقامة, and its reason is like the reason of استعانة.

mekki-muskil:45-45.t: His words {وَاسْتَعِينُوا}: its analogy in its weakening is like نستعين. The hāʾ in His words وَإِنَّهَا لكبيرة refers to the Kaʿba; it is also said that it rather refers to the seeking of help (al-istiʿāna). The seeking of help is indicated by His words وَاسْتَعِينُوا, and the Kaʿba is indicated by His mention of prayer. It is also said that it rather refers to the prayer, and this is the clearest of the views because of its proximity to it. The hāʾ in His words إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُون refers to Allah, Exalted is His mention; it is also said that it rather refers to the meeting, because of His words ملاقوا رَبهم.

mekki-muskil:283-283.t:
His saying {فرهان مَقْبُوضَة}: فرهان is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "then pledges taken in hand suffice in place of that". رهان is the plural of رهن, like بغل and بغال. Whoever reads فرُهُن, it is the plural of رهان, like كتاب and كتب; and whoever makes the hāʾ quiescent does so for lightness. It has been said that رهن is the plural of رهن, like سقف and سقف.
His saying {فليؤد الَّذِي اؤتمن أَمَانَته}: the yāʾ that is pronounced in الَّذِي in the reading of Warsh is a replacement of the quiescent hamza which is the fāʾ (first radical) of the verb in اؤتمن; and the yāʾ of الَّذِي was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as it is dropped when the hamza is lightened.
His saying {فَإِنَّهُ آثم قلبه}: آثم is the khabar of إن, and قلبه is nominative by its verb, namely الآثم [Translator's note: i.e. as its fāʿil (agent)]. It is also permissible to put آثم in the nominative as mubtadaʾ, with قلبه nominative by its verb and standing in place of the khabar, and the sentence is the khabar of إن. It is also permissible to make آثم the khabar of إن and قلبه a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in آثم, and it is a badal of the part from the whole. Abū Ḥātim allowed the accusative of قلبه by آثم, then (also) its accusative as tafsīr (specification), and that is far-fetched because it is definite.

mekki-muskil:284-284.t: His saying {فَيغْفر لمن يَشَاء ويعذب من يَشَاء}: whoever reads it in the jussive conjoins it to يُحَاسِبكُمْ, which is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the condition. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Aʿraj that they read it in the accusative by an implied أَن, and it is a conjunction according to the meaning, as we set out earlier regarding فيضاعفه: the fāʾ is for conjoining a maṣdar (verbal noun) to a maṣdar, taken according to the first meaning, and we have explained it. ʿĀṣim and Ibn ʿĀmir read it in the nominative, as cut off (qaṭʿ) from the first.

mekki-muskil:285-285.t:
His saying {كل آمن بِاللَّه}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). آمن is singular because it is taken according to the wording of كل; had it been taken according to the meaning, He would have said آمنُوا.
His saying {رَبنَا}: an annexed vocative (munādā muḍāf).
His saying {سمعنَا}: its meaning is "we have accepted what You commanded us". From it is the saying of the one praying, سمع الله لمن حَمده, i.e. He accepted his praise from him; its wording is the wording of a statement and its meaning is supplication and request, like your saying غفر الله لي, whose meaning is "O Allah, forgive me".

mekki-muskil:286-286.t:
His saying {لَا تُؤَاخِذنَا}, وَلَا تحمل علينا and وَلَا تحملنا: the wording of all of it is the wording of prohibition and its meaning is request, and it is jussive (majzūm).
His saying {واغفر لنا} {وارحمنا} {فَانْصُرْنَا}: the wording of all of it is the wording of the imperative and its meaning is request; it is indeclinable (mabnī) on the pause (sukūn) according to the Basrans and jussive according to the Kufans. Al-Akhfash reported that أَخذه الله بذلك and واخذه are two dialectal forms.

mekki-muskil:48-48.t: His words {وَاتَّقوا يَوْمًا لَا تجزي}: يَوْمًا is the object of اتَّقوا. لَا تجزي and the clauses after it beginning with لَا are all adjectives (ṣifāt) of يَوْم, and with each clause there is an omitted pronoun referring to يَوْم; were it not for that, the adjective would not be permitted. Its implied form is "لَا تجزي نفس فِيهِ وَلَا يقبل مِنْهَا شَفَاعَة فِيهِ وَلَا يُؤْخَذ مِنْهَا عدل فِيهِ وَلَا هم ينْصرُونَ فِيهِ" (no soul will avail in it, no intercession will be accepted from it in it, no compensation will be taken from it in it, nor will they be helped in it). It is also said that the implied form is "لَا تجزيه نفس": you make the adverb (ẓarf) an object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), then drop the hāʾ from the adjective clause; dropping the hāʾ is better than dropping فِيهِ. Were it not for assuming these pronouns, you would make يَوْمًا muḍāf (genitive construct) to لَا تجزي, as He said «يَوْم لَا ينطقون» and «يَوْم لَا تملك نفس», and this is frequent; when you make it muḍāf, what follows it is not an adjective of it and you do not need to assume an omitted pronoun of it. The Quran readers have agreed unanimously on giving it tanwīn. We have mentioned the origin of اتَّقوا and its weakening under لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُون.

mekki-muskil:49-49.t:
His words {وَإِذ نجيناكم}, {وَإِذ آتَيْنَا}, {وَإِذ قَالَ مُوسَى}, {وَإِذ فرقنا}: إِذْ in all of these is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to نعمتي, i.e. "and remember when We saved you", "and remember when We parted". He, Glorified is He, enumerates to them His earlier favours upon their forefathers.

His words {آل فِرْعَوْن}: [فِرْعَوْن] is definite and foreign, so it is diptote. The original form of آل is أهل; then the hāʾ was replaced with hamza, so it became أأل; then the [second] hamza was replaced with alif because of the fatḥa before it and its being vowelless. When you diminutivise it, you return it to its origin and say أهيل; al-Kisāʾī reported أويل. When you pluralise it you say آلون. As for الْآل meaning the mirage, its plural is أَوال on the pattern أَفعَال.

His words {يسومونكم} are in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from آل. يذبحون is also a ḥāl from آل, or, if you wish, from the pronoun in يسومون; and likewise ويستحيون نساءكم.

mekki-muskil:51-51.t:
His words {وَإِذ واعدنا مُوسَى}: [مُوسَى] is مفعل, from أوسيت; it is also said that it is فعلى, from مَاس يميس. The sīn takes fatḥa in the sound plural on both views according to the Basrans, to indicate the dropped alif. The Kufans said: if you make it فعلى, you give the sīn ḍamma in the nominative plural and kasra in the accusative and genitive, as with قَاض.

His words {أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَة}: its implied form is "تَمام أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَة" (the completion of forty nights), so it is a second direct object.

His words {ثمَّ اتخذتم الْعجل من بعده}: the second object of اتخذ is omitted, and likewise in His words باتخاذكم الْعجل; its implied form is "ثمَّ اتخذتم الْعجل من بعده إِلَهًا" (then you took the calf, after him, as a god).

His words {وَأَنْتُم ظَالِمُونَ} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in اتخذتم; and likewise وَأَنْتُم تنْظرُون is in the position of the ḥāl from the pronoun in أخذتكم.

His words {من بعده}: the hāʾ refers to Moses. Muqātil said: it refers to the departure of Moses, upon him be peace.

mekki-muskil:54-54.t: His words {إِنَّه هُوَ التواب الرَّحِيم}: what is said about إِنَّه هُوَ is like what is said about إِنَّك أَنْت الْعَزِيز الْحَكِيم: هُوَ is like أَنْت.

mekki-muskil:55-55.t: His words {جهرة}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in قُلْتُمْ.

mekki-muskil:58-58.t:
His words {رغدا} are like the first [occurrence].

His words {سجدا} are a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ادخُلُوا.

His words {حطة} are the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "سؤالنا حطة" (our request is remission) or "رغبتنا" (our desire), and the like. It is also said that it is a quotation: they were commanded to say it in the nominative, so they quoted it; had you made the verb of saying govern it, you would have made it accusative.

His words {خطاياكم} are the plural of خَطِيئَة. Its original form according to al-Khalīl is خطائئ: the first hamza is a replacement for the augment yāʾ in خَطِيئَة, and the second hamza is the lām (third radical) of the word; its pattern is فعائل. Combining two hamzas in one word was felt to be heavy, and the word is a plural, which is heavy, so the augment yāʾ was transposed after the hamza that is the lām of the word, so it became خطائي, with a hamza followed by a yāʾ. Then the yāʾ was replaced with alif, a necessary replacement heard from the Arabs in this pattern of the plural, so the hamza took fatḥa and it became خطاءا. So two alifs combined with a hamza between them, and the hamza was replaced with yāʾ, so it became خَطَايَا. Its pattern is thus فعالا, converted from فعالي, transposed from فعائل. Sībawayh holds that there is no transposition in it, but rather that the second hamza, which is the lām of the word, was replaced with yāʾ and then replaced with alif; so its pattern according to Sībawayh is فعالى, converted from فعائل. Al-Farrāʾ said: خَطَايَا is the plural of خطية without hamza, like هدية and هدايا.
[Translator's note: the edition prints the original form as «خطائي» both times; the first, al-Khalīl's starting form with two hamzas, is given here as خطائئ to match the explanation.]

mekki-muskil:61-61.t:
His words {يخرج لنا مِمَّا تنْبت الأَرْض}: the object is omitted, its implied form being "يخرج لنا مَأْكُولا" (bring forth for us something to eat). It is also said that the object is مَا and من is redundant (zāʾida).

His words {من بقلها} are a badal (substitute) for مَا with repetition of the genitive particle; the first من is partitive and the second is for specification, according to Ibn Kaysān.

His words {الَّذِي هُوَ أدنى}: it is said that the alif is a replacement for a hamza, from الدناءة (baseness); on this view the alif in أدنى is a replacement for a hamza. It is also said that it is from الدون (inferior), its original form being أدون, then transposed. It is also said that it is from الدنو, i.e. "nearer", so it is from دنا يدنو.

His words {مصرا}: it is only declinable because it is indefinite; it is also said: because it is a name for the land (balad), so it is masculine. Al-Kisāʾī said: it is declinable because of its lightness.

His words {مَا سَأَلْتُم}: مَا is in the position of the accusative as the noun (ism) of إِن.

mekki-muskil:62-62.t: His words {من آمن}: من is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and is conditional; فَلهم is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and it is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of إِن. It is also permitted to make من a badal (substitute) for الَّذين, in which case the condition is void, because what precedes a condition does not govern it; the fāʾ in فَلهم then enters as an answer to the vagueness, just as it enters with الَّذِي: you say «إِن الَّذِي يَأْتِيك فَلهُ دِرْهَم» (whoever comes to you, he gets a dirham), and Allah, Exalted is His mention, said «قل إِن الْمَوْت الَّذِي تفرون مِنْهُ فَإِنَّهُ ملاقيكم». If you make من a mubtadaʾ, there must be something omitted referring to الَّذين from their khabar, its implied form being "من آمن مِنْهُم" (whoever of them believes).

mekki-muskil:63-63.t: His words {مَا آتيناكم}: the pronoun referring to مَا is omitted, its implied form being "مَا آتيناكموه". مَا is accusative by خذوا, and مَا means الَّذِي.

mekki-muskil:64-64.t: His words {فلولا فضل الله}: فضل is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "فلولا فضل الله عَلَيْكُم تدارككم" (were it not that the grace of Allah upon you overtook you). According to Sībawayh it may not be made overt; it was dispensed with because the speech indicates it. لكنتم is the answer of لَوْلَا.

mekki-muskil:65-65.t: His words {خَاسِئِينَ} are a second khabar (predicate) of كَانَ. If you wish, you may make it a naʿt (adjective) of قردة, and if you wish, a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in كونُوا. The hāʾ in His words فجعلناها refers to the apes; it is also said that it rather refers to the transformation (al-maskha) indicated by the address; and it is also said that it rather refers to the punishment indicated by the speech. Likewise the disagreement about the hāʾ in يَديهَا and مَا خلفهَا.

mekki-muskil:68-68.t:
His words {ادْع لنا رَبك}: the dialect of the Banū ʿĀmir is ادْعِ لنا with kasra on the ʿayn [Translator's note: as written; the ʿayn here is the third radical of the imperative ادْعُ], because it is vowelless and the dāl before it is vowelless — as though they consider the ʿayn to be the lām (final radical) of the word and make it jussive. It is a jussive verb according to the Kufans and indeclinable (mabnī) according to the Basrans.

His words {لَا فارض}: its nominative is permitted by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "لَا هِيَ فارض" (she is not old); it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of بقرة. Like it is وَلَا بكر, and like it is لَا ذَلُول.

His words {عوان} are nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "هِيَ عوان" (she is middle-aged). It may also be a naʿt of بقرة, but by an implied mubtadaʾ is better because of the distance of the noun qualified.

mekki-muskil:69-69.t: His words {يبين لنا مَا لَوْنهَا}: مَا is interrogative, nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لَوْنهَا is the khabar (predicate). يبين does not govern it, since what precedes an interrogative does not govern it. Had you made مَا redundant (zāʾida), you would put لَوْنهَا in the accusative, as Allah the Exalted said «أَيّمَا الْأَجَليْنِ قضيت»: you put الْأَجَليْنِ in the genitive by أَي being made muḍāf (genitive construct) to it, مَا is redundant, and you make أيا accusative by قضيت.

mekki-muskil:70-70.t: His words {وَإِنَّا إِن شَاءَ الله لَمُهْتَدُونَ}: إِن is conditional, and its answer is إِنَّا and what it governs. Al-Mubarrad said: the answer is omitted.

mekki-muskil:71-71.t:
His words {تثير الأَرْض}: تثير is in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in ذَلُول. وَلَا تَسْقِي الْحَرْث is in the position of the naʿt (adjective) of the cow; or, if you wish, you may make it the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "وَلَا هِيَ تَسْقِي الْحَرْث" (nor does she water the tillage).

His words {مسلمة} are the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "هِيَ مسلمة" (she is sound).

His words {لَا شية فِيهَا} are a second khabar of the implied هي. If you wish, you may make لَا شية فِيهَا in the position of the naʿt of the cow, and likewise مسلمة. The original form of شية is وشية; then the wāw was dropped, as it was dropped from يشي, whose original form is يوشي, and the kasra of the wāw was transferred to the shīn in شية.

His words {الْآن جِئْت بِالْحَقِّ}: الْآن is an adverb (ẓarf) for the time you are in. It is indeclinable (mabnī) because it differs from everything else that has the alif and lām, since they entered it neither for prior reference (ʿahd) nor for the genus. It is also said that the original form of آن is أَوَان; then they replaced the wāw with alif, and one of the two alifs was dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.

mekki-muskil:73-73.t: His words {كَذَلِك يحيي الله الْمَوْتَى}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:74-74.t: His words {لما يتفجر مِنْهُ}, {لما يشقق}, {لما يهْبط}: مَا in all of these is in the position of the accusative by إِن; the lāms are lāms of emphasis, and the prepositional phrase (al-majrūr) is the khabar (predicate) of إِن.

mekki-muskil:75-75.t:
His words {أفتطمعون أَن يُؤمنُوا لكم}: أَن is in the position of the accusative, its implied form being "فِي أَن يُؤمنُوا" (in that they would believe); when the genitive particle was dropped, the verb passed on to it directly and made it accusative. The Kufans said: أَن is in the position of the genitive by the implied genitive particle assumed in it. The same disagreements apply to أَن wherever it occurs when a preposition is dropped with it.

His words {يسمعُونَ كَلَام الله}: يسمعُونَ is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, and مِنْهُم is a naʿt (adjective) of فريق.

His words {وهم يعلمُونَ} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يحرفُونَ.

mekki-muskil:76-76.t: His words {ليحاجوكم}: the lām is the lām of kay (purpose), which makes the verb accusative by an implied أَن. It is the genitive lām that enters on nouns, and the implied أَن with the verb is a maṣdar (verbal noun); so it enters in form on the verb and in meaning on the noun. The Banū al-ʿAnbar give the lām of kay fatḥa, and some grammarians say its origin is fatḥa, and that is why it takes fatḥa with a pronoun in your saying «هَذَا لَك», «لَهُ», «لَهُم», «لكم». Most of them say its origin is kasra, for the reason we gave earlier regarding the bāʾ in بِسم الله, and that it only takes fatḥa with a pronoun because kasra followed by ḍamma followed by wāw is felt to be heavy; and also because the speech has no verb in it, so it takes fatḥa with the pronoun for that reason.

mekki-muskil:78-78.t:
His words {وَمِنْهُم أُمِّيُّونَ} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and لَا يعلمُونَ is a naʿt (adjective) of أُمِّيُّونَ.

His words {إِلَّا أماني} are an exception not of the same kind as what precedes (i.e. disconnected).

His words {وَإِن هم إِلَّا يظنون}: إِن means مَا (not), and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ and khabar; إِلَّا is for affirming [the exception to] the negation. Wherever you see a lightened إِن with kasra followed by إِلَّا, إِن means مَا, as in «إِن الْكَافِرُونَ إِلَّا فِي غرور» and its like wherever it occurs.

mekki-muskil:79-79.t: His words {فويل للَّذين} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It is permitted to put ويل in the accusative by an implied verb, in the sense of "may Allah bind upon them woe". ويل is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from which no verb is used, because its fāʾ (first radical) and ʿayn (second radical) are weak letters. It is among the evidence that verbs are derived from maṣdars; had the maṣdar been derived from the verb, as the Kufans said, a verb would be found for this maṣdar from which it was derived. Like it are وَيْح and وَيْس.

mekki-muskil:81-81.t:
His words {بلَى من كسب}: بلَى is equivalent to نعم (yes), except that بلَى is only ever an answer to a preceding negation, and نعم is only ever an answer to a preceding affirmation. The hāʾ in أحاطت بِهِ خطيئته refers to من; it is also said that it refers to the earning. من is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and is conditional; أُولَئِكَ is a second mubtadaʾ, أَصْحَاب النَّار is its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of من. وهم فِيهَا خَالدُونَ is a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from أَصْحَاب or from النَّار, according to the disagreement on that whose explanation has preceded.

Like it in the explanation is {وَالَّذين آمنُوا} up to His words {خَالدُونَ}.

mekki-muskil:83-83.t:
His words {لَا تَعْبدُونَ إِلَّا الله}: its implied form according to al-Akhfash is "أَن لَا تعبدوا" (that you worship not); when أَن was dropped, the verb became nominative (indicative). It is also said that it is an oath, its meaning being "by Allah, you shall not worship".

His words {إحسانا} are a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "أَحْسنُوا إحسانا" (do good, a doing of good). It is also said that it is an object, in the sense of "اسْتَوْصُوا بالوالدين إحسانا" (take to heart good treatment of parents).

His words {لَا تَعْبدُونَ} are [also said to be] in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from بني إِسْرَائِيل, i.e. "We took their covenant, they being monotheists". Like it in all its analyses is لَا تسفكون.

His words {وَقُولُوا للنَّاس حسنا}: its implied form is "قولا ذَا حسن" (a speech possessing goodness), so it is a maṣdar. Whoever reads with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ and the sīn [حَسَنًا] makes it a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "قولا حسنا" (a good speech). It is also said that the two readings are two dialectal forms of an omitted maṣdar [Translator's note: as written; presumably "two dialectal forms, [both] of an omitted maṣdar" or "two dialectal forms of the maṣdar" is meant].

mekki-muskil:85-85.t:
His words {ثمَّ أَنْتُم هَؤُلَاءِ}: أَنْتُم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is تقتلون أَنفسكُم, and هَؤُلَاءِ is in the position of the accusative by an implied أَعنِي (I mean). It is also said that هَؤُلَاءِ means الَّذين, so it is the khabar of أَنْتُم and what follows it is its ṣila (relative clause). It is also said that هَؤُلَاءِ is a vocative, i.e. "يَا هَؤُلَاءِ" (O you), but Sībawayh does not allow this. It is also said that هَؤُلَاءِ is the khabar of أَنْتُم and تقتلون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from أولاء that cannot be dispensed with, just as the naʿt (adjective) of a vague noun (mubham) cannot be dispensed with; likewise its ḥāl. Ibn Kaysān said: أَنْتُم is a mubtadaʾ and تقتلون is the khabar, and هَؤُلَاءِ entered to single out those addressed, since they were alerted to the state in which they persisted.

His words {تظاهرون}: whoever reads it without doubling has dropped one of the two tāʾs; the one dropped is the second according to Sībawayh and the first according to the Kufans. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] allowed أَسارى with fatḥa on the hamza, like سكارى, but Abū Ḥātim disallowed it; al-Mubarrad allowed أسراء, like ظرفاء. It [أُسَارَى] is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun in يأتوكم.

His words {وَهُوَ محرم عَلَيْكُم إخراجهم}: هُوَ is an allusion (kināya) to the report and the matter (the pronoun of the matter), a mubtadaʾ; الإخراج is a second mubtadaʾ and محرم is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of هُوَ; in محرم there is the pronoun of the deputy agent (al-mafʿūl alladhī lam yusamma fāʿiluhu) referring to الإخراج. If you wish, you may make محرما nominative as a mubtadaʾ with no pronoun in it, and إخراجهم its deputy agent, filling the place of the khabar of محرم, the clause being the khabar of هُوَ. If you wish, you may make هُوَ refer to the expulsion because تخرجُونَ was mentioned before, with محرم as its khabar and إخراجهم as a badal (substitute) for هُوَ. It is not permitted that هُوَ be a separating pronoun (fāṣila), since nothing precedes it. This is like the words of the Exalted {قل هُوَ الله أحد}, i.e. "the true matter is: Allah is One".

His words {فَمَا جَزَاء}: مَا is interrogative, nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and جَزَاء and what follows it is its khabar. If you wish, you may make مَا negative.

His words {وَيَوْم الْقِيَامَة}: an adverb (ẓarf), accusative by يُردون.

mekki-muskil:89-89.t: His words {وَلما جَاءَهُم كتاب}: the answer of لما is omitted, its implied form being "نبذوه" (they cast it away) or "كفرُوا بِهِ" (they disbelieved in it). It is also said that the recited كفرُوا بِهِ is the answer of both the first and the second لما.

mekki-muskil:90-90.t:
His words {بئْسَمَا اشْتَروا}: مَا is in the position of the nominative by بئس, and أَن يكفروا is a badal (substitute) for مَا, in the position of the nominative. It is also said that أَن is a badal for the hāʾ in بِهِ, in the position of the genitive. It is also said that it is in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject). The Kufans said: بئس and مَا are a single noun in the position of the nominative. Al-Akhfash said: مَا is indefinite and its position is accusative as tafsīr (specification). It is also said that مَا is indefinite and اشتروا بِهِ أنفسهم is a naʿt (adjective) of مَا, and أَن is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ or by an implied mubtadaʾ, just as you say «بئس رجلا ظريفا زيد» (how bad a witty man is Zayd). Al-Kisāʾī said: the hāʾ in بِهِ refers to an implied مَا, and the overt مَا is in the position of the accusative and indefinite, its implied form being "بئس شَيْئا مَا اشْتَروا بِهِ" (how bad a thing is that for which they sold).

His words {بغيا أَن ينزل}: بغيا is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). أَن is in the position of the accusative by the dropping of the preposition from it, its implied form being "لِأَن ينزل الله" (because Allah sends down).

mekki-muskil:91-91.t: His words {مُصدقا} are a corroborative ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida, circumstantial) from الْحق. Were it not corroborative, the speech would not be permitted, just as «هُوَ زيد قَائِما» (he is Zayd, standing) is not permitted, because Zayd may be without standing while remaining Zayd; whereas the truth is never without confirming the books of Allah.

mekki-muskil:94-94.t:
His words {خَالِصَة} are the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ. If you wish, you may make it accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الدَّار and make عِنْد الله the khabar of كَانَ.

His words {إِن كُنْتُم صَادِقين} are a condition, and what precedes it is its answer.

mekki-muskil:96-96.t: His words {وَمَا هُوَ بمزحزحه من الْعَذَاب أَن يعمر}: هُوَ is an allusion (kināya) to أحدهم, a mubtadaʾ (subject), and أَن يعمر is in the position of the nominative because it is a fāʿil (agent) which you make nominative by مزحزح, and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of هُوَ. It is also permitted that هُوَ be an allusion to the long life (taʿmīr), a mubtadaʾ, with أَن يعمر a badal (substitute) for هُوَ and بمزحزحه the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The Kufans allowed هُوَ to be the pronoun of the unknown (majhūl), a mubtadaʾ meaning the report and the matter, with what follows it a mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of the khabar of هُوَ; but the entry of the bāʾ in بمزحزحه prevents this interpretation, because the majhūl pronoun is only explained by clauses free of genitive particles.

mekki-muskil:100-100.t: His words {أَو كلما}: the wāw according to Sībawayh is a conjunctive wāw upon which the interrogative alif has entered. Al-Akhfash said: the wāw is redundant (zāʾida). Al-Kisāʾī said: it is أَو, whose wāw has been vowelled for ease; there is no analogical basis for this view. كلما is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and the operator on it is a verb indicated by نبذه.

mekki-muskil:101-101.t: His words {كَأَنَّهُمْ}: the kāf is a particle of comparison with no position in i'rab, and the position of the clause is the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of فريق.

mekki-muskil:102-102.t:
His words {يعلمُونَ النَّاس} are in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from الشَّيَاطِين, or from the pronoun in كفرُوا, which is more fitting and better, i.e. "they disbelieved while teaching people magic". If you wish, you may make it a second khabar (predicate) of لَكِن in the reading of whoever doubles the nūn; and if you wish, you may make يعلمُونَ a badal (substitute) for كفرُوا, because teaching magic is disbelief in meaning.

His words {وَمَا أنزل على الْملكَيْنِ}: مَا is in the position of the accusative, conjoined to السحر, or to مَا in His words وَاتبعُوا مَا. It is also said that it is a negating particle, i.e. nothing was sent down upon the two angels in Babylon.

His words {فيتعلمون} are conjoined to يعلمَانِ. It is also said that its implied form is "فَيَأْتُونَ فيتعلمون" (so they come and learn). It is not permitted that it be the answer to His words فَلَا تكفر. It is also said that it is conjoined to يعلمُونَ, but Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] disallowed this. This is a question that needs examination and investigation of the meanings by which the i'rab is completed; the best is that فيتعلمون be resumptive.

His words {لمن اشْتَرَاهُ}: من is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar is مَاله فِي الْآخِرَة من خلاق: من خلاق is a mubtadaʾ, with من added to emphasise the negation, and لَهُ is the khabar of that mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of من. The lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (inchoation), which is the lām of emphasis; it cuts off what follows it from what precedes it, and what precedes the lām does not govern what follows it — like the interrogative particle and like the nouns that make the conditional jussive, which are governed only by what comes after them. Of this kind are the words of the Exalted {وَسَيعْلَمُ الَّذين ظلمُوا أَي مُنْقَلب يَنْقَلِبُون}: أَي is accusative by يَنْقَلِبُون, not by سيعلم.

mekki-muskil:103-103.t:
His words {وَلَو أَنهم آمنُوا}: أَن is in the position of the nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being "وَلَو وَقع أَيْمَانهم" (if their oaths had occurred) [Translator's note: as written; إيمانهم (their faith) is evidently intended]. It is proper for لَو to be followed by a verb, either implied or overt, because it contains the meaning of a condition, and a condition is more fitting with a verb. Likewise His words وَإِن أحد من الْمُشْركين استجارك: أحد is nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being "وإن استجارك أحد من الْمُشْركين استجارك". Likewise, according to the Basrans, إِذا السَّمَاء انشقت, إِذا السَّمَاء كورت [Translator's note: as written; the Quranic text is «إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ»], إِذا السَّمَاء انفطرت and the like are all nominative by an implied verb, because إِذا contains the meaning of requital (mujāzāt, condition), so it is more fitting with a verb; the verb is implied after it, and it is what makes the noun nominative. This is frequent in the Quran, so know it. لَو must have an answer, implied or overt. لَو does not make the verb jussive despite the meaning of condition in it only because it differs from the conditional particles: it does not turn the past into the sense of the future as the conditional particles do, since a condition is only with the future; so it was prevented from governing for that reason.

His words لمثوبة are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and خير is its khabar (predicate); the lām is the answer of لَو.

mekki-muskil:104-104.t: His words {رَاعنا} are in the position of the accusative by the verb of saying. Whoever gives it tanwīn makes it a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "do not say [something of] folly (ruʿūna)".

mekki-muskil:105-105.t: His words {من خير من ربكُم}: خير is in the position of the nominative as the deputy agent (mafʿūl lam yusamma fāʿiluhu) of ينزل, and من is redundant (zāʾida) to emphasise the negation. In من ربكُم, من is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya) and is attached (mutaʿalliq) to ينزل.

mekki-muskil:106-106.t: His words {مَا ننسخ من آيَة أَو ننسها}: مَا is conditional and is in the position of the accusative by ننسخ; من is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and the position of آيَة is accusative by ننسخ. أَو ننسها is conjoined to ننسخ, and نأت بِخَير مِنْهَا is the answer of the condition (jawāb al-jazāʾ).

mekki-muskil:108-108.t: His words {كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَى}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "سؤالا كَمَا…" (a questioning like…).

mekki-muskil:109-109.t:
His words {كفَّارًا} are the second object of يردونكم; or, if you wish, you may make it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in يردونكم.

His words {حسدا} are a maṣdar (verbal noun). In His words من عِنْد أنفسهم, من is attached (mutaʿalliq) to حسد; so it is permitted to pause at كفَّارًا, and one does not pause at حسدا. It is also said that it is attached to ود كثير, in which case one pauses neither at كفَّارًا nor at حسدا.

mekki-muskil:111-111.t: His words هودا: the plural of هائد, which means the repentant. It is also said that هود is a singular, made singular according to the form of من. Al-Farrāʾ said: the origin of هود is يَهُودِيّ, then it was shortened; no analogy supports this view.

mekki-muskil:113-113.t: His words {كَذَلِك قَالَ الَّذين}, in both places: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "قولا مثل ذَلِك قَالَ الَّذين" (a saying like that, those … said). They may also both be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with what comes after ذَلِك as the khabar (predicate). مثل قَوْلهم is accusative by قَالَ; or, if you wish, you may make it a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar.

mekki-muskil:114-114.t:
His words {أَن يذكر فِيهَا اسْمه}: أَن is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) for مَسَاجِد, and it is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). It is also said that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

His words {إِلَّا خَائِفين} are a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative pronoun in يدخلوها.

mekki-muskil:117-117.t: His words {كن}: فَيكون — whoever reads it in the accusative makes it an answer to كن, though this is far-fetched in meaning; whoever reads it in the nominative cuts it off, in the sense of "فَهُوَ يكون" (and it is). We have explained this more fully than here in Sūrat al-Naḥl.

mekki-muskil:119-119.t: His words {بشيرا وَنَذِيرا} are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the kāf in أَرْسَلْنَاك.

mekki-muskil:121-121.t: His words {الَّذين آتَيْنَاهُم الْكتاب يتلونه حق تِلَاوَته}: الَّذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate) is أُولَئِكَ يُؤمنُونَ بِهِ; يتلونه is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكتاب or from the accusative pronoun in آتَيْنَاهُم. It is not permitted that the khabar be يتلونه, because you would be asserting that everyone who was given the Book recites it as it should be recited, and they are not so — unless we make those given the Book the prophets, in which case that is permitted. حق تِلَاوَته is a maṣdar (verbal noun), or a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, and this is better.

mekki-muskil:123-123.t: His words {وَاتَّقوا يَوْمًا لَا تجزي} are like the first in the omission of the pronoun from the adjective clause, attached or detached. The origin of اتَّقوا has already been given.

mekki-muskil:126-126.t:
His words {وارزق أَهله من الثمرات من آمن مِنْهُم بِاللَّه}: من is a badal (substitute) for أَهله, a badal of part for whole.

His words {قَالَ وَمن كفر}: من is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "and I will provide for whoever disbelieves, and I will give him enjoyment". It is also permitted that من be conditional, its accusative being by an implied verb after it, i.e. "and whoever disbelieves, I will provide for", with فأمتعه as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), made nominative because of the entry of the fāʾ. It is also permitted that من be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with فأمتعه as its khabar (predicate), the speech also being a condition and its answer.

mekki-muskil:130-130.t:
His words {إِلَّا من سفه نَفسه}: i.e. "فِي نَفسه" (in himself); it became accusative when the preposition was dropped. It is also said that سفه means "was ignorant of" and "lost", so it is transitive and makes نَفسه accusative. Al-Farrāʾ said: نَفسه is accusative as tafsīr (specification).

His words {وَإنَّهُ فِي الْآخِرَة لمن الصَّالِحين}: فِي is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something implied, its implied form being "وَإنَّهُ صَالح فِي الْآخِرَة لمن الصَّالِحين" (and he is righteous in the Hereafter, among the righteous). It is not good to attach فِي to الصَّالِحين, because that would involve placing part of the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative. It is also said that His words فِي الْآخِرَة are an explanation placed in advance of that. It is also said that the alif and lām in الصَّالِحين do not mean الَّذِي but are only for definiteness, so it is good for the preposition to precede it, being attached to it even though placed before it.

Mujāhid, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī and others read «وإله أَبِيك» in the singular form. It may be a singular, with إِبْرَاهِيم a badal (substitute) for it and إِسْمَاعِيل and إِسْحَاق conjoined to it; or أَبِيك may be a sound plural, with the names after it made badal for it, or إِبْرَاهِيم made accusative by an implied أَعنِي (I mean) with what follows conjoined to it. They are nouns that are diptote because of foreignness and definiteness. The plural of إِبْرَاهِيم is براهيم and of إِسْمَاعِيل سماعيل; it is also said براهمة and سماعلة, the hāʾ being a replacement for a yāʾ. Al-Mubarrad said: their plurals are أباره and أسامع, and أباريه and أساميع. As for إِسْرَائِيل, its plural is أساريل; the Kufans said أسارلة and أساريل.

mekki-muskil:133-133.t: His words {إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا} are a badal (substitute) for إلهك; or, if you wish, you may make it a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it.

mekki-muskil:134-134.t: His words {تِلْكَ أمة قد خلت} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and قد خلت is a naʿt (adjective) of أمة. Likewise لَهَا مَا كسبت is also a naʿt of أمة; it may also be cut off, with no position in i'rab.

mekki-muskil:135-135.t: His words {بل مِلَّة إِبْرَاهِيم}: مِلَّة became accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "بل نتبع مِلَّة إِبْرَاهِيم" (rather, we follow the religion of Abraham). حنيفا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from إِبْرَاهِيم, because the meaning of "rather, we follow the religion of Abraham" is "rather, we follow Abraham". It is also said that it became accusative by an implied أَعنِي (I mean), since the ḥāl does not occur from the muḍāf ilayhi.

mekki-muskil:138-138.t: His words {صبغة الله} are a badal (substitute) for مِلَّة إِبْرَاهِيم. It is also said that it is accusative by incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "follow the dye (صبغة) of Allah", i.e. the religion of Allah. It is also said that صبغة is accusative as a tamyīz (specification).

mekki-muskil:143-143.t: His words {وَإِن كَانَت لكبيرة}: كَبِيرَة is the khabar (predicate) of كَانَ, and the noun (ism) of كَانَ is latent (muḍmar) in it, i.e. "and the turning towards the Sacred Mosque was indeed a great thing". إِن means مَا and the lām means إِلَّا.

mekki-muskil:147-147.t: His words {الْحق من رَبك}: i.e. "هُوَ الْحق" (it is the truth) or "هَذَا الْحق" (this is the truth), so it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). If you wish, you may make it nominative as a mubtadaʾ and imply the khabar, its implied form being "الْحق من رَبك يُتْلَى عَلَيْك" (the truth from your Lord is recited to you) or "يُوحى إِلَيْك" (is revealed to you), and the like. It is reported from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read الْحق in the accusative, making it accusative by يعلمُونَ.

mekki-muskil:148-148.t:
His words {وَلكُل وجهة هُوَ موليها}: وجهة is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and لكل is the khabar (predicate), i.e. "and for every community there is a qibla". هُوَ موليها is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, i.e. "Allah turns them towards it"; so the second object of مولي is omitted.

His words {هُوَ} are the pronoun of the name of Allah, Exalted is His mention. It is also said that it is the pronoun of كل, i.e. "he turns himself towards it".

As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, هُوَ مولّاها, nothing omitted is assumed in the speech, because the verb has passed on to two objects in the wording: one of them is a latent pronoun standing in place of the agent, the deputy agent (mafʿūl lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), and the second is the hāʾ and alif, and both refer to الوجهة. It is also said that the hāʾ is for the maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "made to turn the turning", and the lām in لكل is attached (mutaʿalliq) to مولى and is redundant (zāʾida), like its redundancy in «ردف لكم», i.e. ردفكم; and هُوَ is the pronoun of فريق (party) or قبيل (tribe) or the like, as though He said "the party is made to turn towards every direction", i.e. "made to turn every direction". This implied form is on the view of whoever makes the hāʾ refer to the maṣdar.

mekki-muskil:151-151.t: His words {كَمَا أرسلنَا}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "اهتداء مثل مَا أرسلنَا" (a being guided like Our sending) or "إتماما مثل مَا أرسلنَا" (a completing like Our sending), because before it is تهتدون and before that ولأتم, so you may refer it to the maṣdar of whichever of the two you wish. If you wish, you may make it a naʿt of the maṣdar of اذكروني, though that is far-fetched because it comes before it. And if you wish, you may make the kāf in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf and mīm in عَلَيْكُم.

mekki-muskil:154-154.t:
His words {أموات بل أَحيَاء}: both are nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject) for each, i.e. "هم أموات بل هم أَحيَاء" (they are dead; nay, they are alive).

Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him, read «فَلَا جنَاح عَلَيْهِ أَن يُطَاف بهما». Its [i.e. يطّوّف's] original form is يتطوف on the pattern يتفعل; then the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was replaced with ṭāʾ and the ṭāʾ was assimilated into it, and the wāw was turned into alif because it was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa. [Translator's note: the edition's text is as given; the sentence on the original form appears to refer to the reading يَطَّافَ, and the author calls the tāʾ of the تفعّل pattern "the tāʾ of iftiʿāl".]

mekki-muskil:158-158.t: His words {فَمن تطوع}: من may be conditional, so the position of تطوع is jussive, its meaning is future, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is فَهُوَ خير لَهُ. Or من may mean الَّذِي, so that تطوع is a past verb in its proper sense, and the fāʾ entered in فَهُوَ because of the meaning of vagueness in الَّذِي. This is on the reading of whoever reads the ṭāʾ without doubling. As for whoever doubles it and reads with yāʾ [يَطَّوَّعْ], من is conditional and nothing else, and the verb is jussive by it.

mekki-muskil:161-161.t: His words {أُولَئِكَ عَلَيْهِم لعنة الله}: لعنة is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and عَلَيْهِم is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of أُولَئِكَ. Al-Ḥasan read «عَلَيْهِم لعنة الله وَالْمَلَائِكَةُ وَالنَّاسُ أَجْمَعُونَ», conjoining الْمَلَائِكَة and النَّاس to the position of the name of Allah, because it is in the position of the nominative, its implied form being "أُولَئِكَ يلعنهم الله" (those, Allah curses them), just as you say «كرهت قيام زيد وَعَمْرو وخَالِد» (I disliked the standing of Zayd, ʿAmr and Khālid), putting ʿAmr and Khālid in the nominative because Zayd is in the position of the nominative, in the sense of "I disliked that Zayd, ʿAmr and Khālid should stand".

mekki-muskil:162-162.t: His words {خَالِدين فِيهَا} are a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in عَلَيْهِم. Likewise لَا يُخَفف عَنْهُم الْعَذَاب is a ḥāl from the pronoun in خَالِدين. Likewise وَلَا هم ينظرُونَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the ḥāl from the pronoun in خَالِدين, or from the pronoun in عَنْهُم. If you wish, you may make لَا يُخَفف and what follows it cut off from what precedes, with no position in i'rab.

mekki-muskil:163-163.t: His words {وإلهكم إِلَه وَاحِد} are a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and إِلَه is a badal (substitute) for إِلَهكُم [Translator's note: as written], i.e. "your object of worship is one object of worship", just as you say «عَمْرو شخص وَاحِد» (ʿAmr is one person).

mekki-muskil:165-165.t:
His words {يحبونهم} are in the position of the ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يتَّخذ, and the pronoun refers to من; so it is singular according to the form of من, while من is put in the plural in يحبونَ, referring it back to the meaning of من. If you wish, you may make it a naʿt (adjective) of أنداد; and if you wish, you may make it in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of من, by making من indefinite. All of this is only good because there are two pronouns in it, one referring to الأنداد and the other to من, and من is [referred to by] the pronoun in يتَّخذ.

His words {كحب الله}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a love like your love of Allah".

His words {أَن الْقُوَّة لله}: أَن is in the position of the accusative by يرى in the reading of whoever reads with yāʾ, يرى meaning يعلم (knows), and أَن fills the place of the two objects. If you wish, you may make يرى from seeing with the eye, so that أَن is its object. The answer of لَو is omitted, its implied form being "لندموا" (they would regret) or "لخسروا" (they would lose).

As for whoever reads ترى with tāʾ, it is from seeing with the eye; it is not permitted to be in the sense of "you knew", because [أَن] would then have to be a second object, and the second object in this category is the same as the first, and the matter is not so. The address is to the Prophet, upon him be peace; الَّذين ظلمُوا is the object of ترى and أَن is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). It is also said that أَن is in the position of the accusative by an implied verb indicated by لَو, since it requires an answer, so its answer is what makes [أَن] accusative, because its implied form is "وَلَو ترى يَا مُحَمَّد الَّذين ظلمُوا حِين يرَوْنَ الْعَذَاب لعَلِمت أَن الْقُوَّة لله جَمِيعًا" (if you could see, O Muḥammad, those who did wrong when they see the punishment, you would know that all power belongs to Allah), or "لِتَعْلَمُوا أَن الْقُوَّة لله".

The operator on إِذْ is ترى. إِذْ only came here, though it is for the past, while the meaning of the speech is about the future, because reports of the Hereafter from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are like things that have already taken place, because of the certainty of their occurrence and the firmness of their coming to be according to what the Truthful One — there is no god but He — has reported. So it is permitted to report them with the past, since in the certainty of their being they are like a thing that has already been and passed. This is frequent in the Quran.

The operator on the second إِذْ is شَدِيد الْعَذَاب, i.e. "Allah is severe in punishment when [they] disown". It is also permitted that the operator be an implied verb, i.e. "remember, O Muḥammad, when [they] disowned". It is like the first in إِذْ occurring for the future, while its meaning for which it was coined is the past.

mekki-muskil:167-167.t:
His words {كَمَا تبرؤوا منا}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "تبرّؤا مثل مَا تبرءوا منا" (a disowning like their disowning of us). It may also be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronouns in تَبرأ [i.e. نتبرأ], its implied form being "فنتبرأ مِنْهُم مشبهين تبرأهم منا" (so that we may disown them, resembling their disowning of us).

His words {كَذَلِك يُرِيهم الله}: the kāf is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "الْأَمر كَذَلِك" (the matter is thus); on this view it is good to pause at it and to begin with it. It is also said that the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar, its implied form being "رُؤْيَة مثل ذَلِك يُرِيهم الله" (a showing like that Allah shows them); then one neither pauses at it nor begins with it. حسرات is accusative as a ḥāl, because يُرِيهم is from seeing with the eye; it is a ḥāl from the hāʾ and mīm in يُرِيهم. Had it been from knowledge, حسرات would be a third object.

mekki-muskil:168-168.t: His words {حَلَالا طيبا} are a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted object, i.e. "eat something lawful and good of the food that is on the earth". It is also said that its implied form is "كلوا مِمَّا فِي الأَرْض أكلا حَلَالا طيبا" (eat of what is on the earth with a lawful, good eating).

mekki-muskil:170-170.t: His words {أَو لَو كَانَ آباؤهم}: the wāw is a conjunctive wāw, and the alif is for rebuke; its form is the form of the interrogative. The answer of لَو is omitted, its implied form being "أَو لَو كَانَ آباؤهم لَا يعْقلُونَ شَيْئا وَلَا يَهْتَدُونَ يتبعونهم على خطاياهم وضلالهم" (even if their fathers understood nothing and were not guided, would they follow them in their sins and their error?).

mekki-muskil:171-171.t: His words {إِلَّا دُعَاء ونداء} are accusative by يسمع. {صم} is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "هم صم" (they are deaf).

mekki-muskil:173-173.t:
His words {إِنَّمَا حرم عَلَيْكُم الْميتَة}: مَا is a restraining (kāffa) mā that restrains إِن from governing, and الْميتَة and what follows it are accusative by حرم. Had you made مَا mean الَّذِي, you would imply a hāʾ with حرم and put الْميتَة and what follows it in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إِن.

His words {غير بَاغ} are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in اضْطر. بَاغ and عَاد are like قَاض.

mekki-muskil:175-175.t: His words {فَمَا أصبرهم على النَّار}: مَا is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what follows it is its khabar (predicate). It may be interrogative, and it may be exclamatory (taʿajjub): Allah makes the believers wonder at the disbelievers for doing deeds that bring them near to the Fire; and such is also the meaning of the interrogative.

mekki-muskil:177-177.t:
His words {لَيْسَ الْبر أَن توَلّوا}: الْبر is the noun (ism) of لَيْسَ and أَن توَلّوا is the khabar (predicate). Whoever reads الْبر in the accusative makes أَن توَلّوا the noun of لَيْسَ.

His words {وَلَكِن الْبر من آمن بِاللَّه}: الْبر means الْبَار (the righteous person), or means الْبَرّ (the righteous), so it is من in meaning. It is also said that the implied form is "وَلَكِن الْبر برّ من آمن بِاللَّه" (but righteousness is the righteousness of whoever believes in Allah), then the muḍāf was omitted, and the first بر is the same as the second. It is also said that the implied form is "وَلَكِن ذَا الْبر من آمن" (but the one possessing righteousness is whoever believes), then the muḍāf was likewise omitted. Whoever doubles the nūn of لَكِن makes الْبر accusative, and the implied forms remain as they are. These implied forms were only needed so that it would be valid for the mubtadaʾ (subject) to be the same as the khabar, since concrete beings (juthath) are not predicated of maṣdars (verbal nouns), nor maṣdars of them.

His words {والموفون} are conjoined to the pronoun in آمن, or to من in His words من آمن. It is also said that they are nominative by an implied وهم (and they are), as praise of those referred to by the pronouns, the praise being included in the ṣila (relative clause).

His words {وَالصَّابِرِينَ} are accusative by an implied أَعنِي (I mean), or by conjunction to ذَوي الْقُرْبَى. If you conjoin it to ذَوي الْقُرْبَى, it is not permitted to make والموفون nominative except by conjoining it to the pronoun in آمن, so that it is included in the ṣila of من; you do not make it nominative by conjunction to من, nor by وهم, because you would be separating the ṣila from the relative. So you conjoin والموفون to the pronoun in آمن, and then you may conjoin وَالصَّابِرِينَ to ذَوي. If you make الصابرين accusative by أَعنِي, it is permitted to conjoin الموفون to من and to the pronoun in آمن, and to make it nominative by وهم.

His words على حبه: the hāʾ refers to the believer who gives the wealth, and the object is omitted, i.e. "despite his love for the wealth". It is also said that the hāʾ refers to the wealth, i.e. "and the man gave the wealth despite love of the wealth": the maṣdar was made muḍāf (genitive construct) to the object, just as you say «عجبت من أكل الْخبز زيد» (I wondered at Zayd's eating of the bread) [Translator's note: the edition reads «الْخَبَر» (the report), evidently for «الْخبز» (the bread)]. It is also said that the hāʾ refers to the giving. If the hāʾ is for the believer, it is permitted to make ذَوي الْقُرْبَى accusative by الحب, i.e. "despite the believer's love for the near of kin"; on the other view you make ذَوي الْقُرْبَى accusative by آتى. It is also said that the hāʾ refers to Allah, Exalted is His mention, i.e. "and he gave the wealth out of love of Allah"; the pronoun refers to Allah because He was mentioned before in His words من آمن بِاللَّه.

mekki-muskil:178-178.t: His words {فَمن عُفيَ لَهُ من أَخِيه شَيْء}: the hāʾ in لَهُ refers to من, and من is the noun for the killer; likewise the hāʾ in أَخِيه. The brother is the guardian (walī) of the one killed, and شَيْء refers to the blood. It is also said that من is the noun for the guardian, the brother is the killer, and شَيْء refers to the blood-money (diya) and the forgoing of retaliation. شَيْء is indefinite because it is in the position of عَفْو (a pardon), and عفو is indefinite.

mekki-muskil:180-180.t:
His words {الْوَصِيَّة للْوَالِدين}: الْوَصِيَّة is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "then upon you is the bequest". Making it nominative by كتب is far-fetched, because it would then govern إِذا; and if إِذا is in the ṣila (complement) of الْوَصِيَّة, the ṣila would have been placed before the relative. The deputy agent (al-mafʿūl alladhī lam yusamma fāʿiluhu) of كتب is implied, indicated by الْوَصِيَّة; its implied form is "كتب عَلَيْكُم الإيصاء إِذا حضر" (the making of a bequest is prescribed for you when [death] approaches). So الإيصاء governs إِذا, and what precedes إِذا is its answer; and إِذا and its answer [are] the answer to the condition in His words إِن ترك خيرا [Translator's note: the edition reads «وَإِذا وجوابها وَجَوَاب الشَّرْط», which appears corrupt; translated in the evident sense]. Al-Akhfash said that the fāʾ is implied with الْوَصِيَّة and it is the answer of the condition, as though He said "فَالْوَصِيَّة للْوَالِدين" (then the bequest is for the parents).

If you make الْوَصِيَّة a noun that is not a maṣdar (verbal noun), it is permitted to make it nominative by كتب. It is not permitted that كتب govern إِذا, because the prescription was not written upon the servant at the time of his death; rather it is something that preceded in the Preserved Tablet. The making of a bequest is what occurs when death approaches, so it is what governs إِذا. Al-Naḥḥās allowed making الْوَصِيَّة nominative by كتب on the basis that you assume it after the word الْمَوْت and make it and what follows it the answer to the condition, so that it is intended to come earlier. This is far-fetched: it is not permitted for a thing to be in its proper place and rank and be intended for another place. Also, there is nothing in the speech to govern إِذا if you make الْوَصِيَّة nominative by كتب. There is something to be examined in it.

His words {حَقًا} are a maṣdar. In ordinary speech the nominative is permitted, in the sense of "هُوَ حق" (it is a duty).

mekki-muskil:183-183.t:
His words {كَمَا كتب على الَّذين}: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "كتبا كَمَا كتب" (a prescribing as it was prescribed) or "صوما كَمَا كتب" (a fasting as it was prescribed). It may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الصّيام, its implied form being "كتب عَلَيْكُم الصّيام مشبها لما كتب على الَّذين من قبلكُمْ" (fasting has been prescribed for you resembling what was prescribed for those before you). It may also be in the position of the nominative as a naʿt of الصيام, since it is general in wording and its explanation comes only in what follows it. If you make the kāf a naʿt of الصوم, you make أَيَّامًا معدودات accusative by الصّيام, because it is all included in its ṣila (complement). It is not permitted to make أَيَّامًا معدودات accusative by الصّيام on the other analyses of the kāf, because you would be separating the ṣila from the relative, since the kāf and what follows it would not be included in the ṣila of الصّيام; and if you make أيّاما accusative by الصّيام while it is included in the ṣila of الصّيام, you have separated the ṣila from the relative. Rather, you make أَيَّامًا accusative by كتب, making it an object by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa). If you make الْأَيَّام accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), the operator on it being الصّيام, all that was disallowed when you made الْأَيَّام a direct object becomes permitted, because there is latitude with adverbs, and abstract meanings may govern them, and objects are not like that. There is disagreement over permitting that with adverbs.

The hāʾ in His words {فَمن بدله} and the three hāʾs after it refer to الإيصاء (the making of a bequest), since الْوَصِيَّة indicates الإيصاء. It is also said that they rather refer to the prescribing (al-katb), because كتب indicates الكتب.

mekki-muskil:184-184.t:
His words {فَعدَّة} are nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "فَعَلَيهِ عدَّة" (then upon him is a number [of days]). Had it been accusative in ordinary speech, it would be permitted, on the implied form "فليصم عدَّة" (let him fast a number).

His words {فديَة} are nominative as a mubtadaʾ and the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "فَعَلَيهِ فديَة" (then upon him is a ransom). Whoever gives it tanwīn makes طَعَام a badal (substitute) for فديَة; whoever does not give it tanwīn makes الفدية muḍāf (genitive construct) to طَعَام.

mekki-muskil:185-185.t:
His words {شهر رَمَضَان} are nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and الَّذِي أنزل فِيهِ الْقُرْآن is its khabar (predicate). Whoever reads it in the accusative does so by incitement (ighrāʾ), i.e. "fast the month of Ramadan", with الَّذِي as its naʿt (adjective). It is not permitted to make it accusative by تصوموا, because you would be separating the ṣila (complement) from the relative by the khabar of أَن, namely خير لكم.

The hāʾ in His words أنزل فِيهِ الْقُرْآن refers to شهر رَمَضَان in two senses. One of them is that the meaning is "in which the Quran was sent down to the lowest heaven all at once", so فِيهِ is an adverb (ẓarf) for the sending down of the Quran. The second is that the meaning is "concerning whose obligation the Quran was sent down", just as you say "Allah has sent down Quran concerning ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her"; then فِيهِ is not an adverb for the sending down of the Quran, but rather the verb passes on to it by a preposition, as in His words «وَاهْجُرُوهُنَّ فِي الْمضَاجِع», i.e. because of their staying away from the beds: فِي الْمضَاجِع is not an adverb for the forsaking, but rather a cause of the forsaking, so the forsaking passes on to it.

His words {هدى للنَّاس وبينات} are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from الْقُرْآن.

His words {فَمن شهد مِنْكُم الشَّهْر}: الشَّهْر is accusative as an adverb and cannot be a direct object, because شهد here means being present in the city; the implied form is "فَمن حضر مِنْكُم الْمصر فِي الشَّهْر" (whoever of you is present in the city during the month).

His words {ولتكملوا الْعدة}: i.e. "Allah wills that you complete the number". It is also said that the meaning is "and [He did that] so that you may complete the number"; on this view the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to an implied verb at the beginning of the speech or at its end.
